text: During hot work activity, there was fire incident which impacted two contractor personnel. The more severely injured person was transferred to a specialist burn centre, but he unfortunately passed away.

A floorman was working at a BOP maintenance area at jack up cellar deck at a height of almost 17 meters from the platform top deck. After assembling the BOP shear rams, some housekeeping activities (including tools recovery and collection) were being performed by a crew of total six members. At the time of the incident, the IP was standing on the walking area of the BOP nearby the Coflex (right side of BOP). He had previously received some tools from height in order to recover them (at least a metal plate and a chain block, with total weight of approximately 15 kg) from one crew member standing on the left side of BOP, third floor. The IP approached the right side of the area, through the walking area around the BOP - passing in the rear side of BOP itself. Most likely his intention was to approach the BOP first floor from the right side to collect other tools or to place the received ones in a dedicated area, before the final collection. In any case he put his foot above the Coflex hose connected with the BOP (inherently slippery) and fell down through an open area of almost 1 metre (between the tubular handrail and the walking area around the BOP) from a height of 17 metres. The falling dynamic is compatible with both hypothesis: either the IP lost his balance due to the weight of the tools (approximately 15 kg) or while approaching the BOP first floor. A medevac was immediately activated but the IP was declared dead in the hospital.

During a drilling operation, began to connect drill pipe columns. After the second column was connected and the hook rose to the second floor of the derrick, the driller moved the column to the drill pipe box for operation. When the derrick man was ready to place the column but had not opened the elevator valve, the traveling block hook suddenly dropped, and the elevator fell off and fell to the drill floor, hitting the driller who was working in the wellhead area. His safety helmet was dropped, and the IP fell unconscious on the spot. The operation was immediately stopped and first aid was carried out. The injury was fatal.

During Preventive Maintenance (PM) of emergency shutdown valve at a wellsite, the actuator of the valve abruptly burst and its metallic part hit a nearby contractor. The injured Person (IP) was taken to the clinic, where he passed away. The actuator detached parts hit the flow line Pressure Differential Transmitter (PDT) tubings, which resulted in minor crack on a Down Stream (D/S) welded nipple. This led to gas leakage.
On 26th January 2022, a contractor security guard was killed during a terrorist attack. Some parts of the facility were also damaged by the terrorist.

A Contractor's water tanker rolled over while it was travelling towards a right of way from a water point. There were two passengers in the tanker; a driver and a local person. Both were seriously injured during the accident. Medical treatment was provided to the local person at the hospital. The local person had been engaged by the deceased driver on the day of accident. The driver passed away while he was being transferred to hospital by ambulance.

There was an explosive incident while conducting an under-rig-floor slickline operation. The explosion resulted in one fatality and two injured persons. All of the affected personnel work for contracted companies.

Two divers were involved in an incident during underwater hull repair project for a Floating Production and Storage & Offloading (FPSO) vessel at an offshore production field. The work was conducted at seat with depth of 6 meters (approximately 20 feet). The divers left a Diving Support Vessel (DSV) to perform an adapter mating test. While positioning the adapter in its intended location, the adapter suddenly lost its buoyancy and sank. One of the divers (Diver 1) was seen sinking together with the adapter to a depth of 55 meters (approximately 180 feet), entangled with the adapter rope. Diver 2 rescued Diver 1 and swam up together with unconscious Diver 1 to the surface. Diver 1 was taken to DSV compression chamber, but had lost vital signs at that point. He was pronounced dead four hours after CPR was attempted to revive him.

A fire incident occurred at an offshore production platform during hot work activity inside a pressurized habitat for deck plate replacement near a Booster Compressor Suction Scrubber involving contractor personnel. The fire incident has resulted in 1 one fatality after 3 three days of treatment at a burn intensive care unit, and 1 one burn injury.

During lifting activity on rig site, a TGB joint box disconnected while lifting a pipe that was not centred properly. The TBG joint box suddenly disconnected from the saver sub pin and fell on the work floor. The TBG joint struck the Subcontractor Personnel's head, causing a fatal injury.

During pre-move operations, the IP (a banksman) was caught between an oilfield truck and a tool basket. The IP was initially treated on site by the rig medic, then transferred to the clinic, stabilized, and transferred to Hospital. Incident investigation on going. Driver D&A results were negative.
A fire occurred at a gas plant heater. Emergency Response, Support and Security teams dispatched immediately to the incident location. The incident resulted in 3 injured persons.

During rig move and rigging down operations, the drilling crew was dismantling the TDS. The task was to disconnect the TDS from the guide beam by disengaging the tie-back hook pins. Two Floormen were assigned to remove the upper tie-back hook pins while the Derrickman was to remove the lower tie-back hook pins. Three of the four tie-back hook pins were successfully disengaged, and when the Derrickman was detaching the last tie-back hook pin, the TDS skid swung towards the Floorman's (IP 1) position and struck him against the mast beam. IP # 1 sustained fatal chest injuries. Simultaneously, at the rig floor, the Assistant Electrician (IP 2) was working with the Instrumentation Technician to remove and lower the disconnected TDS service loop cables from the rig floor to the ground. While the Instrumentation Technician pushed the cable away from the handrail, the jerking motion accelerated by gravity made the TDS service loop cable hit IP # 2, who was standing nearby, resulting in IP # 2 losing his balance and falling approximately 40 feet to the ground. IP 2 sustained a fatal head injury.

The operation was dismantling the rig in preparation for a marine move. After disconnecting the monkey board from the mast, the rig crew were moving the monkey board from beneath the mast. The monkey board was resting vertically on the ground on its front side guardrails and a crane's fast line was connected to the monkey board pad eye and kept under tension. The crew were using the crane fast line on off-driller side and two forklifts diagonally. The crane operator slacked the fast line wire completely and as the monkey board was engaged by forklift # 2, the monkey board tipped over onto the floorman (IP), causing a fatal injury.

An old hose hangar made of metal frame (weighing approximately 240 kg) was kept in a vertical position at the main deck STBD side area beside a pipe rack. While the service company well testing supervisor was locating a spare elbow in the area, the frame became unbalanced and fell, hitting the IP on his neck, leading to a fatal injury.

A vehicle (double cabin pickup) was carrying five occupants when the driver lost control and the vehicle deviated from the road and collided with a 48" fire water line and went through the gap underneath the line. This resulted in fatal injuries to the driver and a passenger, and three passengers sustained serious injuries. Emergency response teams along with medics responded and rescued and transfer casualties to the medical centre. HEMS were activated and the injured were evacuated to hospital. All three injured persons were treated and later discharged from hospital.

An electrical helper was pulling out a piece of unistrut channel piled on a scaffolding rack at a laydown area. While pulling out the channel, the scaffolding rack collapsed on him causing fatal head injuries.
Contractor crew was attempting to connect a tractor to a conveyor belt trailer. A contractor worker walked behind the conveyor belt trailer and was caught between the trailer and the blender.
A contractor employee was fatally injured when he was struck by the counterweights while working on a pumpjack isolation.

On December 4, 2022, a floorhand on a drilling rig was struck in the head and shoulder by a fold-up walkway that fell from the tubing board while racking back a stand of pipe. The injured contractor was transported by ambulance to hospital, where the IP was listed in critical condition. The IP passed away as a result of his injuries on 6 December 2022.
A drilling crew member sustained a fatal injury after being struck by the "grasshopper" electrical delivery mechanism (also called the umbilical cable tray) while rigging down the drilling rig.

An incident occurred resulting in two fatalities and two injuries. A crew of four people were working on the blind flange connection at a 36" line. Another crew had completed a hydrotest on that same line on July 4th. As the crew was working, the blind flange was displaced. The sudden release of pressure caused injuries that resulted on two fatalities and hospitalization of two other employees. A fifth person who was not part of the crew but located in the same working area was seen at the clinic on site and later released.

A business partner crew completed a pneumatic leak test of the chilled water/return line in the utilities building and then had transitioned to a function test of the flushing equipment. During the flushing equipment function test, one of the temporary 4-inch hoses connected to the chiller system disconnected from its coupling, causing a release of air. Additionally, air was released through a discharge hose that was routed from one of the temporary manifolds to the top of a tank. The hose began to move in an uncontrolled motion as air reached the end of the hose. A crew member evacuating from the chiller room through the western exit was fatally struck by the hose.

Working with heavy vibrating equipment, the operator got down to carry out an unforeseen task between equipment, and the equipment that was coming up behind did not see him and when it started it trapped him.

The incident occurred while the victim was working alone excavating materials at a quarry. The victim called his colleagues to inform them the loading shovel was stuck. His colleagues arrived seven minutes later and found that the quarry wall had collapsed, and the operator was partially buried in his machine. They attempted to assist the victim without success. Death was confirmed later by the medic.
During test operations with flowback equipment from an exploratory well, while routine tasks were being carried out in the high-pressure sand separator area, an unplanned release of energy occurred.
A contracted company employee was walking in an operational area crossing an internal road when he was run over by a forklift. He was promptly rescued but died in the hospital on the same day.

Four workers were carrying out maintenance work in the auxiliary motor generator room when the CO2 fire-fighting system was spuriously activated, flooding the room. Two workers escaped the room in time (without injury/functional disturbance) and the other two workers were rescued by the emergency response team, one of whom died.

A S76 C++ helicopter collided against the water about 900 metres from an oil rig after an inflight loss of control on the final approach to the helideck. After the impact the helicopter assumed an inverted position. The 11 passengers and the co-pilot managed to escape the inverted helicopter. The captain, although rescued by the co-pilot after his absence on the surface was noticed, did not survive.
A forklift overturned while assisting the drilling contractor with extending the mast raising line.

Near miss: Slickline tool dropped. During second run of slickline operations and after setting the lock mandrel in the landing nipple, the contractor operator was in a slickline unit pulling out a toolstring using a joystick handle. When the toolstring reached the surface, the wire did not stop and the toolstring continued going up at full velocity. Therefore, the toolstring hit the upper sheave wheel and the rope socket (connection between wire and toolstring) parted, causing the toolstring to drop from approximately 25 m height and onto the rig floor. No one was on the rig floor when, the incident happened.

There was an Emergency Total Shutdown of the central processing facility. The root cause of this trip was not known, and so electrical and instrument supervisors were brought in to check if there was any problem before proceeding to restart the facilities. During this period and exactly at 06:45 there was gas detection from several gas detectors. A cloud of gas was noticed coming from the old horizontal flare pit. All production wells were immediately shutdown and the facilities depressurized. HSE fire brigade installed water curtains and opened several fire monitors to dilute and disperse the gas cloud. After closing the production wells and depressurizing the facilities, the gas cloud started decreasing until it had disappeared. No Personal injury or asset damage resulted from this event.
While working on digging the foundation for the perimeter fence, one of the technicians touched an underground cable with his shovel spade and saw a spark..

During a rainy period, a closed drainage valve caused rainwater to accumulate on the roof of a tank that favoured the growth of moss and lichen. There were also traces of paint on the tank roof following recent waterproofing work. A team of operators (T1) had been working on the roof of the tank to clean off the moss and traces of paint. The team was using a presumed algaecide/fungicide considered as a specific, multi-surface, grease-removing agent -and equipment (PPE, scrapers, brooms, etc.). Later, a second team (2), which was working on the tank wall, noticed a paint run in their work area. Because they did not have any cleaning agent, they asked team (1) to give them some of the product. Team (2) took what they thought was an empty metal pot of hardener as a recipient for the cleaning agent, in fact containing a residue of hardener and paint from a previous work - and poured part of the cleaning agent into it. When they had finished their task (around midday), the rest of the product that had not been used (around 3 litres) was handed back to team (1). At the end of the day, the remaining product in the metal pot was poured back into a container of the pure product. Exhausted by the heat, the operators left the work area, leaving the equipment and products on site. In the early evening, two firefighters performing their round noticed smoke coming from the tank roof and stepped in to contain the fire outbreak. The container into which the product had been poured had melted and spontaneously combusted. The fire had then spread to the equipment nearby and damaged part of the separating wall on the periphery of the roof. Immediate actions: -Intervention by firefighters and triggering of the deluge system of the tank.

At 15h42, an incident occurred on the Well head (WH) during a routine scraping operation. During the rig down phase, the truck hoisting winch cable broke when lifting the Blow Out Preventer (BOP) from the well head (WH) until its receptacle on the mast. The pressure control equipment (PCE), no longer being held by the lifting cable struck the gangway surrounding the WH and the lubricator tipped over the gangway access ramp to the ground. The gangway guardrails were bent and part of the PCE damaged. The operator standing on the gangway at the BOP side was slightly injured on his right leg by the guide rams. At the clinic, he received some first aid treatment for few minutes and returned to his job. A truck was requested for removing the PCE from the platform, then the well was secured and put back into production.

A wax re-injection project was commissioned to solve the problem of the accumulation of more than 2,000 bbl. of wax at the landfill for several years, by purchasing and installing an electric heater in a merlon to dissolve the wax and re-inject it into the process. On September 14, around 8:15 a.m., a contractor noticed a fire starting inside the wax dissolving merlon located at the level of the pig receiver of the 18" pipeline outlet. The contractor hit the nearby fire extinguisher (water and additive) and then went to the control room to raise the alarm.

At approximately 1:25 a.m., an emergency shutdown of the facility occurred. At the same time, an operator in the area on tour noticed a fire at the crude export pumps. The operator immediately alerted the control room, which triggered the emergency response (1111). The night shift (three staff members) went to the muster point 50 m from the station, as required by the emergency procedure. At approximately 1:35 a.m., the First Response Team (FIT) arrived at the station and after a quick assessment of the risks and the extent of the flames, they decided to attack the fire safely, using the fire extinguishers present in the station. It should be noted that 100% of the fire extinguishers at the site were used and replaced within three days.

In the early morning of Sept 16, 2022, at the processing facility at approximately 00:43 am, a loud noise was heard by the night panel operator, quickly followed by a total shutdown of the station (ESD1). An inspection of the processing facility revealed a damaged piece of equipment was blown 12 m further from the gas compressor. A damage assessment of other equipment was realized, and compressor isolated from the process.
2 1/2" Valve separated from a fire hydrant during deluge testing and landed 9m away.

During a transfer operation of personnel to the platform boat landing by boat, a wave suddenly appeared and unbalanced the boat. As a result, a contractor employee lost his balance when he was boarding on the stairs to the platform, having caught his right foot between the last step of the boat landing and the boat, causing an injury to the front of the right foot. Immediate action: The employee was assisted onsite by colleagues and transferred for first aid treatment provided by the doctor. Due to the suspicion of a fracture, he was referred to hospital for further assessment. Following investigation, the cause was found to be a failure to comply with the embarkation and disembarkation procedure at the boat landing. A video showed that the employee took too long to go up the stairs. The boat assistance in position of letting the waves coming behind. The Captain should have used the 2 option boat landing to control the very smooth waves of that day. Recommendations were set up and implemented to avoid reoccurrence.

A crane operator was running the crane to support the construction project team in the installation of the Mobile crane at a Platform. A signal was given to the crane operator to lower the load block and pick up the king post brace. The load (king post brace) was successfully picked and positioned to the MAST Top section of the king post. In the attempt to socket the king post brace into the mast swivel collar, the team noticed that the upper male clevis of the King post brace would not fit into the swivel collar. The banksman gave a signal to the crane operator to swing right, he successfully swung right and cleared the brace from the MAST top section. The next signal was given to the crane operator to lift the load (King post brace). While the load was hoisting, the crane boom suddenly swung to the left and the load moved above the MAST Top section of the King post. Two employees were standing on the scaffold around the MAST Top section of the King post.

The silencer internals failed, resulting in debris being ejected up to 35m. At the time of the incident, 15 authorized people were within this radius. The closest being 3 valve operators who were standing 22m from the silencer vent. No one was injured from the falling materials.

A worker was struck by pipe movement while operating a manual valve which was being closed to build-up pressure and then opened to clear the piping system of any debris. The incident occurred when the pressure release rapidly causing the spool to shift suddenly, striking the worker.

The heat up preparation was started. One of the activities performed was the removal of the heat up burner (HUB) plug. After the removal of the plug and civil inspection, flash fire incident occurred while waiting for the installation of the heat up burner. One of the contractor partners was caught in the flash fire and suffered a burn injury.
On Tuesday the 17th of May at 3.45pm, electrical work was being undertaken in substation one. A person was involved in fitting an air circuit breaker when they inadvertently contacted live equipment.

On March 16th, a M-8 Helicopter was about to lift a cargo net of 10x200l Fuel Drums at the Base laydown. The load master had connected the cargo net lifting points of the chains, and signalled for the aircraft to lift. As the longline started to become taut the loadmaster started to move away to the safe area and noticed the lifting points of the net dropped with the weight of the chains. When he looked up, he observed the longline falling down in a spiral loop from the aircraft and moved further away to a safe location. The flight engineer advised the captain flying that the hook had released. The captain checked with the load master if he was safe and after confirmation the aircraft returned to the helipad. The 52m longline with load cell (75kg total) came to stop on the ground approximately 7 metres from the load and 6 metres away from the loadmaster. No personnel were injured, and no equipment was damaged.
The tree fell during thunderstorm and broke the window glass and damaged the fence.
An operator performed a petrol site check around the well head then fell into a well cellar.

A marine crew member (IP) was attempting to untangle a bundle of wire rope slings on board an anchor handling vessel. In doing so, the IP stepped backwards and fell into an open chain locker. The chain locker is approximately 7 metres deep, the IP was able to arrest his fall by maintaining his grip on the wire rope sling that he was handling. His grip minimised the impact when he landed at the bottom of the empty chain locker.
Uncontrolled descent of mudlogging unit while being moved by rig crane.

While the personnel were trying to rectify a flow control valve (FCV) that has been hunting, the team identified that the control valve issue was due to the actuator internals soft kit having been worn out. While trying to rectify the actuator by unbolting of the spring retainer, the bolt, spring plate and spring were ejected vertically (under tension), hitting a pipe before landing on the floor grating. No one was injured in the incident as all personnel were consciously avoiding being in the line of fire.

Dropped objects from Telescopic Boom Crane. The crane operator started the engine of a telescopic crane for warming up prior to performing the operation. Suddenly he saw two of the slippers had fallen onto the portside mezzanine deck. The Crane Operator stopped the crane and checked. It was observed that the slippers had fallen from the crane boom to the portside mezzanine deck area close to the survey pool tugger.

At approx. 11:00am, the IP was preparing to carry out derrick inspection. After hooking onto the cable sleeve the IP stepped on the bottom rung of the derrick ladder and put his body weight onto the cable sleeve to test it. This resulted in the wire coming free from the top socket and the IP fell backwards onto the Calvin Slip Bowl which was lying 1.2m west of the bottom of the ladder.

Two pieces of detached ceiling insulation cladding were found on top of a pipe. These claddings were used to hold ceiling insulation. One stainless steel sheet has a weight of 11 kg and another angular stainless-steel cladding has a weight of 13 kg. Dropped height is at around 7-8 metres, which, with the weight of the dropped objects, will qualify for a potential fatality consequence as per the DROPS calculator.

At approximately 16:00 hrs, the operation was stand by on the weather at the shelter area. A Bosun, an Able Seaman (AB) and a cadet were transferring equipment from the ship's office to the ship's garage under the crane along the ship's safe walkway. They observed that the ladder that had previously been secured to the ship's side railing started to become loose and they went out of the safe zone walkway to the side railing to re-secure the steps. At this time there were heavy swells coming past the vessel but they did not observe any coming over the side as they watched for a few minutes. While they started to re-secure the steps and had taken their eyes off the incoming sea, a large swell around 3 - 4m came over the side of the bulwarks of the vessel and hit the ABs (IP). The swell was strong enough for him to lose his footing and he fell on the deck and was pushed down the deck to just forward of the crane pedestal. The Bosun and Cadet came to assist the IP who was unable to get back up due to an injury to his ankles. The IP was carried by stretcher to the sick bay where the IP was assessed by the medic. The Incident happened very quickly, and there is no evidence to show exactly what has caused the injuries to the IP.

Wooden bar support crane boom rest dropped onto platform. On 18 May 2022 at 0700 hrs., after completing crew change activity, while a Production Operator (holding valid crane license class B) was controlling a crane boom to park onto crane boom rest. The wooden bar on the top of the crane boom rest suddenly dropped onto the platform where a rigger was working nearby, approximately 5 metres away from the boom rest.

Gas release from gas lift compressor intercooler. A tube bundle in the gas lift compressor inter-cooler burst and 453kg of hydrocarbon gas was released to the atmosphere. Process Safety Fundamental: Not applicable.
During strong winds three scaffolding planks fell to the ground, a drop of about 23 metres, with an expended energy of 1800 Joules. No one was hit, but there were people in the area.

During inspection, one of the participants bumped into a loose plank stored on the scaffolding. The plank fell into a manhole to the level below. The area was not cordoned off. There were no personnel in the area below.

During installation of the green sea panel by ship side, a steel wedge came out of position and fell down and hit the railing on the quay, bounced and landed on some tarp between the boat and the quay.
Loose cable tray was unsecured on top of existing cable tray. The loose tray fell and landed on gangway. The area was not cordoned off.

A 2.35 m long rail (2.55 kg) for fixing of tarpaulin fell from the underside of the main deck in connection with dismantling of the emergency stair tower at a column by a team of hired scaffolders. The rail hit the scaffolding floor above the pontoon deck approximately 24.5 m below. The pontoon deck was cordoned off, but there were three scaffolders from the dismantling team inside the barriers without paying attention to the work directly above. The rail hit the scaffolding floor less than 0.5 m from one of them, where it made a dent in the scaffolding plank.

While L/D directional drilling BHA, after multi frequency resistivity (MFR) tool was pulled out from well, this tool was secured on one end with winch (wire sling) and on the other end with the crane (wire sling). During L/D operation/moving manoeuvres from the rig floor to the catwalk the tool slipped from the winch and remained hanging just on crane sling. The result was that it fell to the ground with one end close to the catwalk. The directional drilling tool and two casing joints (from the ramp) were damaged.

During welding works at a pipeline located near a saltwater tank, an explosion followed by fire occurred at the saltwater tank. The roof of the saltwater tank was thrown away, damaging a nearby oil tank. Several barracks and equipment were damaged. Also, some third-party buildings in the vicinity were damaged.

An operations team were preparing a 14" pipeline riser for reconnection to a new topside facility service with the cap suitable for the associated axial load. The 14" condensate export line had remained isolated, water-filled, inhibited, and decommissioned since the project hook down phase in 2019. The line was positively isolated at one end and fitted with an engineered cap at the other end. The cap was connected to the riser via a pipe coupling. Both cap and coupling were rated for 10bar service with the cap suitable for the associated axial load. As 100% lower exposure limit was identified when sampling the void space contents at one end, as per local procedure, the team were attempting to perform Nitrogen pressure purges of the 10-metre void space to displace residual hydrocarbon before removal of the cap to allow welding of a connecting pup-spool to the open riser. Whilst trying to locally verify the applied N2 purge pressure, the engineered cap and pipe coupling were vertically ejected. The equipment and debris resulted in physical injuries to three people in the vicinity; Injured Person 1 was lifted upward and fell back to scaffold, Injured persons 2 and 3 suffered minor facial injuries from impact with debris and/or equipment.

When pulling a 13 3/8" Intercept plug (length 9.9 m, weight 2.8 tons) the plug dislodged from the running tool as the tugger wire attached to the lower end started to take load to initiate tailing out the assembly. The lower point of the assembly was at this point approx. 0.5 m above the rig floor. When the plug impacted on the rig floor, it parted and broke into pieces.
After skidding, the drilling rig part of a railing, 1m wide, was to be reinstalled. During installation, the handrail fell to the deck below. Weight of railing part: 35.7 kg. Fall height: 21.5 m.

During backloading of cargo part of a gate on the crane's ring platform fell to the deck below. The port had been fastened using a ratchet strap. A loose end had unintentionally been tangled in the ladder as the crane turned around. Weight of gate part: 1.24 kg. Fall height: 15.7 m.

Rope access climbers were working on a deck rigging up firewater hose for fire monitors. To connect the hose, they needed one more chain hoist to be connected up in order to lift/support the hose while connecting it to the flange. One of the persons in the team connected a webbing sling to the chain hoist and prepared to choke the sling around the deck support beam. The person realized he was not reaching high enough to get the webbing sling around the beam, so he took one step up on the lowest horizontal pipe on the handrail. To stabilize himself, he then took his other foot over the handrail. At this point he was per definition working over the side without any harness.

The oil export pump shaft started to rotate while personnel was working up close to the shaft. The work, adjusting a sensor, had just ended when the shaft started to turn. The rotation of the shaft was caused by the starting of the upstream oil booster pump. This caused the fluid in the line from the booster pump to turn the impeller on the export pump B, causing the shaft to spin. This could happen as there was no mechanical isolation of the oil export pump.
During loading bulk barite on starboard side loading station from supply boat, a lid on the Rock Catcher in the bulk line came loose and landed FWD on the lay down area.

When breaking and laying down 5 1⁄2" HWDP singles a dropped object occurred falling approximately 20 metres from the Tubular Feeding Machine (TFM). The dropped object was one of the TFM's side bumpers which was found inside Red Zone drill pipe setback.
Crush injury. The IP was repairing a link on the drag chain, the drag chain fell 1/2metre and the IP was caught underneath.

A pup-joint dropped uncontrolled approximately 13,7 meters during a lifting operation. The task was to move the pup-joint from the drill floor to a storage rack outside the wind wall. At the same time a person was walking down the stairs under the lifting area. The person was not hit by the falling pup-joint or physically injured.
The lid from a decommissioned open vent line fell on the walkway during heavy winds. Weight of lid: 20 kg. Fall height: 37 m.

Diving operations were ongoing at vessel while lying with the wind to its side to protect the LDC (light diving craft). The FWD thruster was isolated and the turret locked in line with diving isolation matrix. The STB thruster was out of service due to an ongoing upgrade project. The Port thruster was the only thruster in operation and available. In preparation for greasing of the port thruster steering pump 2A, the duty pump was switched from 2A to 1A. Pump 2A shutdown as per logic. Directly after, pump 1A tripped due to low-pressure alarm not clearing after start-up as per logic. The standby pump 2A did not auto-start. This resulted in no azimuth control (direction) of the thruster and loss of heading control of vessel for approx. 10 mins.
Whilst executing a replacement program of constant load supports, or spring cans, a load was dropped to deck. The scaffold lifting frame erected for the task failed.

Contact with pressure gauge on pig receiver during lifting operations. Container being lifted from supply vessel to a restricted landing space made contact with pressure gauge on live pig receiver. No hydrocarbon release occurred.

Unexpected excursion of dive support vessel whist two divers were setting up local rigging. ROV was also at depth. No injuries were sustained, no equipment was damaged. Vessel Dynamic positioning (DP) system based its calculations on false position references leading to a vessel excursion.

While the drilling mechanical crew were on the rig floor aligning Traction Motor A with the draw-works, a jack and a half of iron roughneck roll were being used as a spacer to lift the shaft. During the alignment, the movement caused the iron roughneck roll to slip off and fall through the vent opening of the Traction Motor A. The roll dropped 10 metres to the area below into a barricaded area. No personnel were present in the barricaded area and no injuries or damages resulted from the dropped object. Dropped object weight = 3.4kg.

Coiled tubing operators were in the process of rigging up a Coiled Tubing (CT) Injector Head on a rig's travelling block using a crane. One operator was inside a man basket holding the slings and the other one was standing on the injector head attaching the shackle. After successfully attaching one sling, the CT operators attempted to attach the second sling. While pulling out the shackle pin, it fell approximately 9 m. to the rig floor. The pin was 20 cm long and weighed 5.9 kg.

Top drive system (TDS) link tilt hydraulic cylinders pins and retainer was found near the V-door. It weighed 360 grams and fell from a height of between 10 and 38 metres, as the height it fell from could not be determined precisely.

During rigging down of well testing equipment, an atmospheric storage tank was over pressured using compressed air from a compressor via a manifold. This over pressure blew the tank roof off the body of the tank, which landed in a nearby wastewater pit.

While the floorman was using chain tongs to remove a sub from the drill string, the driller activated the top drive system (TDS) causing the drill string to turn while the floorman was holding the chain tongs. The Floorman was thrown onto the rig floor when the Driller operated TDS.

While the air winch hook was clipped onto the lifting eye bolt on the body of the air winch, the winch then continued to pull up and the air winch pulled itself off the base pedestal welded connection.

Operator initiated the wrong control lever and the auxiliary hook did not stop, which led to the auxiliary hook striking the turn down sheave, flipping over and landing on the back of the boom. The turn down sheave and associated components were damaged.

An 80 ton crane and operator had completed a lifting operation at the production facility for the installation of a new security cabin, and were due to return to the town, when the driver received a call from the crane owner requiring him to relocate both himself and the crane to a well inside our operation block, due to a hose leak identified on an existing crane at the rig site (another crane used at rig site). On route, the crane's brakes started to smoke due to the steep decline from the well site road turning to the base of the mountain, where the driver stopped to let the brakes cool down for approximately 33 minutes. The driver then restarted the crane and continued his journey. The route was a total distance of 31.2 kilometres. The first stop was after 3.1 kilometres calculated from the wellsite turning to the base of the mountain due to the crane's brakes starting to smoke. The driver continued his journey a further 26.1 kilometres over inclining and declining roads before approaching the turning. As the driver reached the turning, he found that the brakes would not function and that the crane was moving too fast to make the right turn. A split-second decision was made to continue down the declining road hoping that the road would level out. The crane driver was unaware that the well site was located 2 kilometres ahead at the bottom of the hill. On approach to the well site, the crane crashed through both the security barrier and perimeter gates, continued across the pad, colliding with two concrete barriers used to protect the flowline, before finally coming to a stop above the flowline after pushing the line off its supporting brackets.

The secondary roof (25m x 9.5m) of the newly constructed laundry building became detached due to extreme high winds, traveling approximately 50m, before landing on the main camp generators, resulting in a minor diesel spill (diesel leak contained within bund and therefore not categorized as a spill).

While lowering the Rig mast, the mast retention slings snapped, causing the traveling block to move from the retention position and hang by the drill line itself in a lower position. High potential of drop object.
A fully loaded brackish tanker slipped backward and got stuck on the edge of the hill while driving to a well location with a high potential chance of rolling over. No injuries reported.

A High-pressure Rental pump has been mobilised to injection well in an attempt to increase the water injection rate using a High Pressure Pump system. During pre-commissioning, a water hose developed a Leak due to the impingent of a high velocity water jet.
Personal injury (laceration) in the right ear while loading plates into the load basket.

The IP was working on 2nd level of port aft leg jacking unit to conduct maintenance activities. His supervisor was preparing tools on deck, and while the IP was about to lift the jerry can of oil over the handrail (approximately 19kg), suddenly the handrail failed, and the IP fell to the deck from a height of approximately 5.5 m. The medic was immediately notified, a stretcher team arrived and transferred the IP to clinic. The IP was conscious but in shock. Urgent MEDEVAC onshore arranged.

Five riggers were assigned to move the gratings one by one from the bundle which was placed vertically on a pallet located nearby the handrail on the walkway of middle deck. The metal strap that held the grating compressed against each other was removed and the grating began to slide on its side. A piece of grating slid from the bundle through the handrails and fell from 19 metre height on the HVAC unit (2 metre height) located at the main deck bounced and fell on the walkway. Two workers were located approximately 5m away from the HVAC Unit. A low-pressure fuel gas line was located approximately 2m away of the impacted area.

The IP was working inside the welding habitat at 1.8m high supported by a scaffolding platform. He was standing on a narrow platform beside an open hole. There were two fire blankets on top of each other near the open hole. IP inadvertently stepped on the fire blanket, slipped and fell through the open hole to the lower deck of the habitat.

While lifting a rotator head, the tugger line snagged on a beam and snapped. The rotator head fell approximately 10ft to the mat, bounced and landed approximately 2ft from a worker. The tugger line also recoiled, went through the crown and fell approximately 120ft to the floor.

During rig out of the service rig, a worker was attempting to coil and stow a temporary electrical cable. The cable end became stuck underneath the catwalk. A worker attempted to pull the cable end free but was unsuccessful. The worker then pushed the cable end in an attempt to free the cable end from the catwalk. The workers right hand (with donned wet glove) made contact with the inner connections (4 pole/208 Volts/60 Amps). The worker reported experiencing a momentary electrical shock. The worker reported pain continuing post shock with tingling sensations. The ground conditions were snow covered with water accumulation in low spots atop frozen ground with temperatures of +5 Degrees Celsius with clear skies.
Two vehicles, a pickup truck and empty tractor trailer, collided on a winter ice road curved corner. Major damage was sustained to the pickup and minor damage to the tractor trailer unit.

A crane was extending their boom out to 70ft to prepare for a personnel lift. When the boom reached approximately 60ft the whip line ball crowned causing the approximately 125lb ball to separate from the cable and drop to the trailer deck, landing approximately 8ft from a worker.

The rig crew and casing crew were in the process of making up a joint of casing when they noticed the backup tongs were on the casing collar and needed to be lowered to the casing joint body. The IP decided to help push the backup tongs down by standing on them. He placed his right hand on the stationary equipment and his left hand on the casing tongs to hold himself steady and push down on the backup tongs. The IP had inadvertently put his left hand on the casing tong door latch and bent his finger down just as the tong operator had started making up the joint of casing. As the casing tong began to turn, the IP's finger was caught between the gear and tong body, severing his left ring finger at the third knuckle (closest to fingernail).

Rig was tripping in the hole, Top Drive raised in the blocks, preparing to make a connection. Floorhand #2 saw Floorhand #1 (Injured Person) struck by a bright object on his upper left arm (Biceps), while standing in the alley / rig floor with a stand of drill pipe in his tailrope. Fallen object is a steel Drag Chain link rod measuring approximately 3/8" wide x 16" long, weighing 396-g (0.873-lbs), and was positively identified as having fallen from the Drag Chain belt from a minimum height of 27.43-m (90-ft) above the rig floor. Injured Person was alert, responsive, and transported to hospital for further evaluation.

A rig contractor was rigging down from a well, and the logistics contractor was in the process of removing the V-door from the substructure. The lifting equipment was secured, with a tagline attached. Pins securing the V door to the substructure were removed to allow lifting and removal of the V-door. As the load was being lifted, the crane reversed, and the load levelled. This created a bind in the load, causing one of the d-rings to dislodge from the lifting hook. The V-door fell approximately 3 metres onto the drill line and managed pressure drilling line below. All personnel were clear of the area at the time of the event, and no injuries were reported.

The boom pole hoist was secured to its tie off point on the casing porch with its handle inadvertently stuck in the hoist position. The hydraulic power unit was engaged, and the boom pole spool began to hoist. The casing porch was lifted from its cantilever support arms until the boom pole hoist cable parted and ended up suspended on one of the arms.

Brakes failed to hold the load allowing an uncontrolled decent of the blocks and tubing. As the load dropped the blocks came to rest against the handrail of the work platform near one of the rig employees.

After night shift completed the blender swap, the 1 inch chemical hose for the biocide was left unsecured inside secondary containment by the blender. While transferring biocide chemical, the chemical hose was turned on releasing an estimated 2 barrels of the biocide chemical inside secondary containment and 14 barrels outside of containment onto the ground.

The rig crew was tripping out of the hole. The rig employee (IE) was pushing an 8" drill collar away from the stump to position it into the racking board. The drill collar became hung up on the derrick board. The IE repositioned and attempted to pull the drill collar into the racking board. As the IE was moving the drill collar, the driller slacked off the winch connected to the collar to help move it around the derrick board. As the drill collar was coming down, the IE's foot slipped on the rig floor. This slip caused his right foot to slide underneath the drill collar as it descended, causing a major injury to the toe.

A flash fire occurred when a contractor, the Injured Person (IP), was blowing down the surface casing pressure. Proper notifications were made, and the location was shut in. The events were as follows:
• Vent off casing gas as part of routine rounds.
• Opened manual valve and flash fire occurred.
• Shut valve and called for help.
• Lead Operator attended to IP.
• IP received medical attention.
Battery fire. Emergency shutdown (ESD) on wells failed to close and water tanks ran over sending fluid to combustor starting initial fire. Process Safety Fundamental: We sustain barriers.
An arc flash occurred while the IP was working on a recloser pole. A permanent impairment injury (PI) occurred.

After performing clean out of transfer line, the IP was checking equipment. The IP was about to climb the ladder to the tank when his 4 gas monitor alarmed. The IP evacuated immediately and notified the supervisor.
Separator end cap failure. End cap on the separator had failed casing release. Process Safety Fundamental: We walk the line.
Parked kill line hose. Kill line hose parted at a crimp connection. Process Safety Fundamental: We apply procedures.
Gas release. Natural gas release. Process Safety Fundamental: We maintain safe isolation.
Work String Failure. Work string failure caused by drill pipe being separated below rotary and within BOP.
Uncontrolled vehicle injury. Worker appears to have left his vehicle in gear after exiting.
Personnel slipped into water in a frac pit. Worker slipped and slid down the pit wall into the water after collecting water samples.

Elevator link described an oscillating movement when lifting top drive. • The steps in the operating procedure with casing running tool equipment are not described.
• In the manoeuvre the portable radius was not used to have good communication between the drilling cabin and the contractor manager.
• The task suspension policy is not effectively applied.
• Raised the Elevator Link with the Winch to remove the catwalk without realizing that the Elevator Link were together and uneven.

During a period of high winds, the wellsite sign became dislodged from the securing frame from which it was mounted on the antenna deck and fell to the deck below. There were no personnel in the area at the time; no other equipment was damaged. The 73lb. sign fell 15 feet, registering as high potential on the DROPS calculator.

While rigging up elevators to 16 foot bails in preparation of the 7 5/8 inch casing pull, the link tilt was kicked out away from well centre by inflating the link tilt air bag to install the secondary safety latch sensor on the elevators. The link tilt air bag ruptured resulting in the 16 foot bails coming to rest on the rig floor. A worker was tasked with installing the safety latch sensor and was positioned in between the elevators and the 7 5/8 inch casing stump. The casing elevators contacted the worker's right shin.

When introducing the plug and perf (PnP) BHA to the Wireline lubricator for stage 25 of the well, the fishing neck got stuck inside the quick-lock device, and due to the over tension the mechanical weak point broke and the BHA fell to ground level (exposure of personnel).
Chain hoists were connected to the bridge crane, the basket was removed and the BOP skid was moved to the East side, causing the derailment and fall of the chain hoist.

During test activities with the PTS pump in a Pulling Rig, the person operating the machine detected that the lever brake system of the hoist did not fully respond and carried out 2 strokes using the equipment's socket/clutch to stop the downward movement. This situation was observed by the Company Man who ordered to stop the task. In order to stop the task and leave the equipment in a safe condition, the operator decided to raise the pipe as much as possible to avoid leaving the pump resting on the bottom and place the pneumatic wedges. As it rose, it reached the end of the stroke, causing the hoist to fall, reaching the bottom, resting on its side and bending the tubing.

While performing tracing and thermal insulation activities over a tank located in a Crude Oil Plant, a sudden ignition and subsequent fire occurred. The fire was controlled by plant firefighting system and the Company's own firefighting team.
During well telemetry maintenance tasks, a short circuit occurred in the frequency inverter in the electrical power input terminal block.

During the monthly/weekly inspection of the lifeboats and the rescue boat (scope of the preventive maintenance program), in the test of the descent brake of the rescue boat, the davit winch cable broke and the boat fell into the sea from an approximate height of 20 metres. The test consists of releasing the boat with braking after approximately 5 metres of descent by gravity. When braking, the cable broke. The boat was unmanned, as per the test procedure. There was no risk of hitting people. There was no rupture of fuel or lubricant tanks.

After replacing the oxygen cylinder of the oxyacetylene set, when the worker opened the cylinder valve, there was an abrupt increase in pressure. At that moment, the pressure regulator and flame arrester could not withstand this sudden increase, causing a burst and spring projection against the workshop wall. The worker was not hit, due to his position on the opposite side of the projection.

During maintenance work on a 3" automatic valve, located at the NGL outlet of a condensate stabilizer (on standby) there was a leak of condensed liquid. During the event, there was no damage to people or assets. This event was classified as a Tier 2 PSE.
During river water filling operation of tank, there was a loss of containment in the walls of the riveted tank, causing the tank to collapse.
During normal operation at the Gas Plant, there was a plant shutdown due to the activation of the safety system.

Worker felt an electrical shock while attempting to relocate a scaffold rack stored on the platform deck. Investigation identified that the scaffolding was rested on two 480V electrical cables that ran the perimeter of the deck. The insulation on one cable was broken, exposing the electrical conductor.

After completion of activities under the scope of a preventive maintenance on Deck Crane B, an employee was preparing to lower materials from the top of the crane. A rope was tied with a single knot to the handles of a tool bag and a plastic bucket, mainly containing tools. At the beginning of the descent movement, when the set was at the crane's upper platform level, it bumped at its guardrail and the knot came loose and the materials fell to the Main Deck, which had not been barriered-off for this crane maintenance. The location of the Main Deck where the objects hit was close to an escape route, being an area of regular and frequent passing of people. Height fall was measured as 17.42 meters and load was weighted as 9.38 kg, resulting in a fall kinetic energy of 1,603 Joules.

Scaffolding tube (4m long) fell from a height of 15 metres with a weight of 14.4 kg onto the main deck in the bow below the flare superstructure. The tube first collided with a guardrail that was on the floor (waiting for installation), hit the floor and, when lying on the deck, brushed against a worker who was in the area. No injury was found to the worker.

An offshore support vessel was near a drilling rig in adverse sea conditions. The vessel's captain was positioned in the forward command, and moved towards the stairs, which gave access to the lower floor. When the vessel rocked he lost his balance going towards the stairs, falling backwards and sliding to the end of the stairs (height 3.2 metres) on the lower floor.
Individual sustained hand injuries when struck by piston during BOP Maintenance Operations.

On 15/06/2022 during the night shift at about 23h00, during POOH, ESP completion, the Operator was in the Rig floor adjusting the spider handling tool to get it back onto its normal working position. His hand's little finger got pinched while lowering the spider into the equipment sleeve, located in the master bushing in the rig floor. He was immediately transferred to the rig doctor's clinic. After examination, the rig doctor decided to transfer the IP to HMD for X-Ray examination and further consultation by a specialist. Amputation of the 3rd phalange of the fifth finger of the right hand. 45 days sick leave.

During a cementing operation, the supervisor noticed that the mix in the concrete mixer was too solid. He asked for more water and pulled the drum up with the hand wheel to prevent the mix from overflowing. One worker helped the supervisor by lifting up the lever to facilitate the manoeuvring of the wheel. Another tried to push the drum up next to the first helper. The IP decided to pull the drum up as well, by positioning himself on the opposite side. When the drum was released and started to rotate again, the IP's left hand was positioned at the gearing, in which three fingers of his left hand were engaged. The IP suffered an amputation of the last phalange of the left index finger, a fracture of the middle finger, and lacerations on the middle and ring fingers.

During a purging operation with Nitrogen on the preserved 14" condensate export pipeline to the platform, the end flange "cap" was dislodged from the pipe end and damaged the scaffolding around. The line has been idle for 3 years with positive isolation. The equipment and debris resulted in physical injuries to 3 people in the vicinity; Injured Person 1 was lifted upward and fell back to scaffold. This resulted in 5 fractures of the spine and permanent partial loss of hearing. Injured persons 2 and 3 suffered minor facial injuries from the impact of the debris and/or equipment. One person was injured during work on cantilever drag chain. Injured person was repairing a link on the drag chain. During this operation, the drag chain fell 1⁄2 m, and injured person was caught underneath. Injured person was transported to hospital. Activated general alarm and mustered personnel.

On 26 March 2022, A scaffolder, working on a gas development, suffered a serious finger injury during operations to de-construct a scaffold tower. A colleague of the injured scaffolder was lowering the scaffold board from a platform at 17m elevation (1) to another colleague on the level below (2) when the scaffold board slipped from his grasp and fell. The injured scaffolder was standing on the 4m elevation platform (3), with his hand on a vertical scaffold-tube post which supported the scaffold hand-railing. The falling scaffold board hit his hand, crushing it against the post and amputating his right index finger. The finger was preserved and surgically re-attached (but it is not fully functional after recovery), such that the injured person was subsequently declared fit to return to work.

While tripping out of the hole, team members were in the process of racking/setting a stand of 5 1⁄2" drill pipe back in the derrick. The injured person lost his balance and extended his right hand out in an attempt to break his fall. During which time, the stand was inadvertently sat down on his right hand with the elevators unlatched from the stand.
Vacuum Truck Driver walked to the cellar to adjust the truck's suction hose when the cement head separated from the casing and impacted their right foot.

After night shift completed the blender swap, the 1-inch chemical hose for the biocide was left unsecured inside secondary containment by the blender. While transferring biocide chemical the hose was turned on releasing an estimated 2 barrels of the biocide chemical inside secondary containment and 14 barrels outside of containment onto the ground. IP reported eye irritation and coughing due to chemical exposure (fumes) from the reported biocide chemical spill that occurred earlier in the morning. IP initiated first aid by flushing his eyes with water. IP felt the chemical exposure was getting worse and reported the incident to the onsite Safety & Environmental (S&E) Rep. IP was escorted by the S&E Rep to the medical facility in the town for medical evaluation.
Arc flash occurred while IP was working on recloser pole. FPI occurred.

At approximately 1:40 PM crew was in the process of removing the tubing hanger and the wrap-around. During the process, the pipe wrench (36) slipped and one of the contractors mis-stepped and injured his leg.

At approximately 10:30 AM, 2 Floorhands were pushing back a stand of 5.5 inch slick, heavyweight drill pipe. Once the pipe was close to where it was going to be set down, momentum let the pipe come back towards the Floorhands pushing on it as it was not set down but low to the ground. As it came back the pin end of the stand contacted the top left foot area of one of the Floorhands' boots causing injury to his left foot. The stand was still latched and not fully set down on the foot. Emergency medical services was notified at 10:31 AM, arrived on location at approximately 11:08 AM, and determined due to potential trauma the injured person was airlifted to hospital.

On Wednesday, June 29, 2022, a surface ops maintenance contractor was working at a tank battery and was injured when a section of piping assembly fell from a vice and pipe rack and struck the contractor in the ankle. The injured person (IP) was transported via air flight to Hospital, where it was determined that the IP suffered two broken bones in his ankle, which was also dislocated. As a result, the IP was admitted to the hospital for surgery to repair the broken bones.

IP was struck in the upper right arm while depressurizing an isolated section of piping in preparation to service a CO injection well meter. The contractor was struck by the 1/2-inch meter assembly piping that parted. The IP was transported to the ER, diagnosed with a right humerus bone fracture, and subsequently admitted to hospital for treatment.

On the afternoon of Wednesday, March 29, an insulation contractor working at the Gas Plant was struck by a sheet of plywood being utilized as a shade shelter. The strong winds lifted the plywood and struck the IP working approximately 50' downwind of the shade shelter. The IP has broken ribs and possible vertebrae fractures. The IP was transported to the ER and subsequently transferred to a Hospital for treatment.

An incident occurred resulting in two fatalities and two injuries. A crew of four people were working on the blind flange connection at a 36" line. Another crew had completed a hydrotest on that same line on July 4th. As the crew was working, the blind flange was displaced. The sudden release of pressure caused injuries that resulted on two fatalities and hospitalization of two other employees. A fifth person who was not part of the crew but located in the same working area was seen at the clinic on site and later released.
Removing the manoeuvring tubing, at substructure, operator proceeds to open the riser to remove the tubing, catching his left index finger between the riser gate and the tubing (2.7/8") wedge.

At approx. 18:30hrs, the Lease hand and motorman were preparing the area to rig up. It was identified that the flare line and some wellhead fencing would need to be moved to allow adequate room for a Blooey line stand. When the Lease hand and motorman moved the fencing panels, the lease hand's middle finger became pinched at the pivot point between two of the connected fence panels. Post treatment the IP had the top section of his middle index finger removed down to the first knuckle.

Whilst loading a gang box into a 10ft container, the spotter assisting the forklift driver attempted to push the gang box into the container. The gang box (weighing approximately 150kg) had dislodged resulting in injury to the spotter's right thumb.

The cattle grid was being removed for cleaning and the injured person (IP) was removing a nut from a stud securing the cattle grid to the mounting with a 30mm ring spanner. While pulling on the spanner, the IP felt the left (L) shoulder pop and was in immediate pain.
Not available.

At approximately 11:20hrs, an offshore tug/supply ship was called to tie up with the rig for backloading operations (casing and basket). After the vessel was in position, the vessel informed the crane operator to lower down the mooring rope for connecting with a bollard. After vessel crews tied up the mooring rope with the bollard, the vessel banksman informed the crane operator by radio to take tension on the mooring rope. The vessel bollard guard came loose from its original position and came into contact with both deck hands.
During Helicopter Underwater Escape Training (HUET) a person hit the helicopter structure in the neck area while moving to the surface after removing the seat belt underwater.

The IP was descending stairs holding the handrail and carrying a single scaffold coupling in the other hand. The IP's left foot slipped on a step and his right leg gave way. He tumbled 3 steps down onto a scaffold platform. The IP was diagnosed with a quadriceps tendon rupture in his right leg requiring surgery.

Person hit by a ROV shackle while assisting in a lifting operation. The shackle was lying on the top of cover, attached to the rigging but not secured to the cover. The slings started to gather on the deck, so the IP moved forward to remove them, not recognising line of fire.

Prior to the installation of the new hook-up spool, a blind lid on a new flowline to well was to be split and removed. Confined pressure was not detected, and pressure was therefore not drained before the split was performed, resulting in lifting a blind lid (34 kg) 1.6 m up in the air. This hit the operator in the face on the return. 2.4 kg HC gas escaped, resulting in gas detection - 2 sensors activated. This led to activation of the deluge system and ESD. One person in the work team was seriously injured.
The IP tripped over temporarily stored equipment, fell and suffered a fractured hip.

Crush damage to finger in connection with release of mooring line from bollard. During "release" of a vessel (vessel
1) on quay, the IP got his fingers caught between the mooring line and the bollard. The mooring line of vessel 1 crossed over the line of vessel 2. They were attached to each bollard. Movement of vessels due to waves led IP to believe that the mooring line was slackened. IP grabbed the line with fingers in and around, which meant that finger got caught between line and bollard.

During the disassembly of the metering valve, an accident occurred during the uncoupling of a 6" valve from the manifold flange. Once the valve was uncoupled, it turned abruptly, trapping the hand of the injured person between the valve handwheel and the manifold, where the worker's hand was resting.
During a fishing operation, while fishing the parted wire, the securing clamp with chain failed under tension and struck and injured the wireline assistant operator's hands.

At approximately 15:25hrs, a Gas Processing Operator was operating the discharge valve of a gas compressor when suddenly the valve packing and handle came out of the valve body, which hit the operator and resulted in hand injuries. The subsequent fall resulted in a face injury. The Gas Plant Control Room notified the emergency services and medical assistance was provided.

Finger injury while inspecting oil leak of generator. The IP decided by himself to stop by the CSP area to have a visual inspection of the leak so that he could determine the full extent of the leakage and seek the necessary repairs from the maintenance team the next day.

Tip of Index Finger amputated during Fender Recovery Operation. While pulling the rope, it suddenly slackened due to the swell, followed by a forceful jerk, leading to the amputation of the tip of the IP's right 2nd digit distal phalanx (index finger) and an open fracture of the 3rd digit distal phalanx (middle finger).

An assistant driller sustained injuries on his left thumb and index finger, while breaking out connection of Bottom Hole Assembly Rig. He was administered first aid at site and then was taken to hospital for further treatment. This resulted in amputation.

While lifting a pump using a crane at a rig site, the load touched the nearby Hydraulic Power Unit (HPU) roof, and the roof fell down and struck the left index finger of a Roustabout, resulting in amputation.

After completing Run in Hole (RIH) 3.5" completion tubing, one pup joint got damaged by the power tong. The decision was made to lay it down. The Power tong operator (IP) (Subcontractor crew) parked the power tong offline and attempted to fix the stuck back up jaw while rig crew were laying down the damaged pup joint. The IP placed his left hand in the backup jaws in an attempt to fully open the stuck back up jaw, while his right hand was on control levers. Suddenly the backup jaw closed and caught two fingers of his left hand (Middle & Ring fingers) resulting in a crush injury.

A contractor worker was using their left hand to steady coil tubing while cutting it above the tubing joint with a hacksaw. When the cut was complete, stored energy in the parted coil drew the parted coil, the clamp, and the tubing joint into the tubing joint below resulting in injury to, and amputation of several fingers.
On Thursday, 6/29, while using a punch to extract a roll pin from the tong make-up head, a small piece of debris went under the safety glasses and into the contractor's right eye.

Contractor crew was preparing for a pipeline tie-in. While performing a bevel cut with a torch to remove a section of pipe, a flash fire and liquid condensate fire occurred resulting in burns to three contractors. IPs were transported to local medical facility for medical treatment and care. 2 were transferred for further treatment and care beyond first aid.

IP was on the new location of rig move and going to check frac tanks for levels of OBM being transferred from the old location. As the IP climbed a JST frac tank, he grabbed onto the top section handrails to assist in climbing the steps. The bolts that normally secure the top section of the handrails were missing, allowing both handrails to pivot back towards the IP when he grabbed them, causing him to fall off the steps to the ground. When the IP landed, he landed on both feet, then fell backwards onto the ground causing pain and soreness to both ankles. The IP was on the step approximately 5'2" from ground level when the incident occurred.

At around 6:00 PM, crew was in the process of swapping out a portable pump at a pond when the IP sustained an injury to his right foot. The IP went to unclamp a high-pressure hose that still had some residual pressure, causing the hose to boost loose and ricochet back, hitting the IP on the right foot and causing an injury to his big toe. The medical case management company was notified and due to the nature of the injury notified the IP to go to Medical Centre to be treated. The IP stated he was wearing steel toe boots when the injury occurred. Upon receiving more information, this incident will be classified as a Recordable Days Away. The IP received a Morphine drip, and stitches to close the laceration. The IP also has a first and 2nd distal phalanx fracture, given a prescription for Cephalexin, and Ibuprofen. The IP is currently on his way to an Urgent Care for further evaluation/follow up.

A crew member was injured while attempting to secure cargo on deck. Crew members were working to secure cargo with chains and binders. The water washing over the stern was pushing a cargo container towards the IP, which struck the IP's lower right leg causing a fracture and leading to permanent reduction of musculoskeletal function.

life_saving_rules: Line of Fire|Bypassing Safety Controls|Energy Isolation
text:
• Ensure proper barriers in place while dealing with high pressure fluids.
• All Operations (Routine and Critical) require competent person to be performed; their knowledge must be formally assessed prior to start any job.
• Stop work authority to be always applied whenever required.

During pipe demolition activity on open drain system, IP positioned their right hand between a spool and existing structure. After the spool was cut, it made a pendulum and stuck the IP's hand against the structure causing a cut and fracture of the 4th and 5th fingers.

Engine boy performed a routine visual check of the engine room of the vessel to support geophysical activity. At one point, a possible oil leak was identified in one of the starboard generator filters. The worker then positioned himself between the bulkhead (wall) of the engine room and the generator, so that he could have a better view of the filter, where the leak supposedly occurred. While he was in that position, the vessel moved suddenly due to the sea conditions. The worker lost his balance and, to avoid falling, tried to hold on, involuntarily placing his hand on the pulley of the water pump that was in operation, suffering amputation of the distal phalanx of the fourth finger of his left hand.

During planned preventive maintenance of the thruster, with it electrically isolated, an employee was assessing the manhole to remove the plug for the lubrication process, when the thruster shaft moved, pinching the distal phalanx of the middle finger of the left hand. After medical evaluation onshore, amputation of the distal phalanx of the 3rd finger of the left hand was confirmed.

During the activity of receiving an 18m-long empty metal basket from the waste management area on an extensive truck with crane on the quayside, the crane operator, in an attempt to avoid what might become a collision against the crane cabin, pushed the basket with his own hand, resulting in a crushing hand injury between the load and the crane rear view mirror.

During the activity of moving cargo on deck to the warehouse on the lower deck, two sailors helped open the hatch lid with their hands. During this process, the piston moved the lid, creating a small space between the lid and the edge of the hatch, enough for one of the sailors' hands to occupy this space, being pressed when the lid unexpectedly returned to its resting position.

The activity on well 2 started on June 17th with the equipment mobilization in location. On June 18th the job officially commenced on site. The Scope of Work was to carry out maintenance activities on Xmas Tree and ambient valve recalibration. Operation was performed with support of Slick Line service and downhole plug. During the activity, the team observed the Slick Line and the upper sheave were not moving. In order to fix the issue, the Contractor Supervisor bled off the pressure in the hydraulic hose of the SL stuffing box through the dedicated hydraulic line, and proceeded to slack the cable at the bottom sheave to resume jar action This brought to failure the pressure equalization across the downhole plug and consequently led to the ejection of the same inside the lubricator which parted and jumped on air. The lubricator ejection determined the Slick Line cable tension and strong knockback. Consequently,the lower sheave, connected to such cable, strongly impacted the IP's chest and chin. IP medical conditions immediately appeared critical. The event led also to a slight gas release.

While a Business Partner A-frame/Floater handler was attempting to disconnect a pipe floater from an 8-inch pipeline to lower the pipe, his arm became trapped, and the weight of the pipeline and the orientation of the floater dragged him under the water.

A contractor convoy was ambushed by unknown gunmen. Four government security personnel and two contractor drivers were fatally injured. Two contractor expats were kidnapped, but were released 17 days later.
A Pusher Tug with Environmental barge experienced an engine room fire. One of the crew sustained severe burns and was admitted to hospital for treatment and later passed away.

Fall from height during scaffolding dismantling at project fabrication site. During the incident, the scaffolder was dismantling the cantilever scaffold when the scaffold frame suddenly tilted after the he stepped onto the ledger box-tie member. This caused the scaffolder to lose his balance and fall onto the ground, together with the scaffolding structure. The scaffolder was observed hooking his full-body harness to the scaffold frame instead of the lifeline.

Contractor bowser, filled with crude oil, left the plant around 3 pm. While commuting from the plant to a refinery, at 10.45 pm, the bowser rolled over and caught fire, resulting in the driver's death. The helper suffered a burn injury and was immediately transported to hospital but later also lost his life.
Terror attack - no further information.
Fatality of a rope access technician whilst performing inspection tasks.
While removing the Christmas tree using air tuggers, the securing bracket for the air tugger failed. This caused the air tugger winch to rotate and fatally crush the IP against a steel I-beam.

On the day of the incident the gathering center was under total shutdown. The job was to replace the corroded 42" tank vapour gas piping. The activity was performed by cold cutting by the contractor. While cold cutting, an explosion and fire occurred that resulted in two contractor fatalities, 12 lost work day cases, and 1 minor injury. Emergency responders attended. The fire was extinguished by fire crew. The employees were transferred to medical facilities by ambulance. The deceased person was taken by Forensic medical department.

When a Production crew was conducting routine well monitoring and troubleshooting, they noticed a spill from a nearby pipeline. The crew approached the spill site to investigate. Upon arriving at the site, the crew saw the water disposal pipeline had failed, and a pinhole was sending high-pressure produced water into the desert sand, creating a five metre-wide and two metre-deep whirlpool. During this observation, one of the workers slipped into the newly formed whirlpool. Crew members made several attempts to rescue him and were finally able to retrieve him from the water. One of the rescuers went into the hole and had to be rescued without any further harm. Emergency Medical arrived on site to begin advanced life-saving techniques but were unsuccessful.

At approximately 2:55 am, a contractor was performing circulation prior to cement on well, when the wellhead started leaking fluid with hydrogen sulphide (H2S) release. A total of 7 people were reported to be impacted (1 deceased, 4 transferred to hospital and stable, 2 examined at site clinic). The well was secured (BOP shut-in) and the location was evacuated.
A contractor was operating a forklift when the forklift contacted an energized overhead power line, causing the death of the contractor and equipment damage.
Worker was managing high fluid levels in the low pressure knock out (LPKO) vessel while bringing wells online at the facility and was found unresponsive.

Company vehicle was traveling in their lane of traffic and was approaching another vehicle going in the opposite direction. The other vehicle was hauling a trailer that was loaded with a compressor. The loaded compressor became loose and fell into the path of the company vehicle. The IP was transported to hospital where they passed away from injuries sustained in the collision.

The driver of a cementing plant truck, lost control and the truck rolled into a ravine. An ambulance and rescue squad called to the scene reported that the driver died at the scene. The machinist passenger suffered a head injury and broken arm and was taken by ambulance to the hospital but died after three hours.

While trying to start unloading new concrete slabs from the vessel and loading them onto the offshore platform, 2 employees of the oil and gas construction trust, a welder and a fitter, fell into the water because of failure of the old concrete slab of the platform. After search and rescue efforts, involving divers, bodies were found and taken out of the water.

A high potential event occurred when unbolting a pressurized flange. During the assembly and disassembly of blind flanges of the cold box bypass, the GTP performing crew were mistaken about bypass flanges pass A 18" and worked on the blind flanges of pass B which were not already isolated and were under nitrogen pressure. When the crew observed a pressure release, they stopped working and left the area. Afterwards, the exploitation operator was in the area, recognized the situation, and quickly opened the vent to depressurize the line.

Driver observed to be unfit and falling asleep while driving. During the journey back to the office (from the base site), passengers were concerned that the driver was not concentrating on his driving and falling asleep at the wheel.

The injured person (IP) was trying to lower the deck during which a moonpool A frame (150kg) was obstructing the path. While attempting to reposition the A-Frame with the chain hoist, the A-Frame fell on the IP, impacting the hard hat and wedging the IP between the A-Frame and pollution tank.
A Hydraulic workover unit (HWU) that was rigged up on top of wellhead fell 49 feet to the ground with 3 workers in the work basket.

At 4:42 pm, as a company rental vehicle was returning to the hotel after purchasing supplies for next day lunch boxes, the driver swerved to miss a child riding a bike. The vehicle left the road, hit a power pole, and rolled over twice before coming to rest on the side of the vehicle. The vehicle's speed immediately prior to the incident was recorded at 106 km/h by the IVMS. The maximum speed limit is 60 km/h. The driver and passenger (member of the public) were picked up by a company vehicle soon after the incident, travelling in the opposite direction and taken to the hospital.
