An employee had just finished lifting a shale bin using two loaders (one with a stinger, chain, and lifting equipment) in order to place matting underneath. Once the matting was in place, the employee directed the loader to lower the bin until there was enough slack in the lifting chain to remove it. As the employee grabbed the eye of the lifting chain to unhook it, the operator of the loader bumped the controls with his knee, causing the chain to tighten and pinch the employee's right middle finger between the bin and the chain. The employee's right middle finger was amputated between the middle and upper joint, and the employee was hospitalized.
An employee's left ring fingertip was caught between the cylinder and motor as he was performing maintenance on a compressor.
An employee was performing duties as a derrick hand at an oil/gas production site when his right index fingertip was pinched and amputated between a pipe and a latch.
An employee was adjusting a press machine when the ram fell and crushed her right ring finger, amputating it at the knuckle.

Employees were using a rough terrain forklift truck to pivot a fork of another rough terrain forklift truck. The fork was tied to its carriage. When the fork was untied it came down and struck an employee standing near the truck and broke his leg near his ankle.
An employee was standing on the edge of a containment wall while changing a pump when he slipped and fell 1.5 feet from the wall and fractured his left forearm.
An employee was picking up cones and warning signs in a road construction area when he was struck by a runaway car, requiring hospitalization.
An employee was getting out of his truck when he slipped on ice/snow, fell to the ground, and broke his left fibula.

An employee was moving a catwalk (a long piece of equipment that helps move tube) against a rig to perform an inspection when his right ring finger was caught and fractured between the catwalk skate and a pin. He was hospitalized.
An employee slipped and fell on ice while walking to a truck, fracturing his right leg.
An employee was using hydraulic controls to lower an iron roughneck when his right pinky finger and knuckle were caught and fractured between the iron roughneck and the hydraulic cat head.

An employee was working on the rig floor of a workover rig. The crew was picking up pipe from the hole. The operator descended the block to the rig floor to connect to the pipe. The bails and elevators were connected to the blocks. When the elevators came down, the employee's finger was caught between the elevator and bail resulting in a left middle finger amputation at the first digit.
An employee was opening a valve he was repairing when he dropped the valve hand wheel. As he tried to catch it, the wheel crushed his middle fingertip, which had to be amputated.

An employee was transferring water at high pressure through a hose. The hose failed and a jet of water knocked the employee through the air approximately 150 feet. When the employee landed on the ground he suffered a shoulder injury.

An employee was working on a blowout preventer. When he went to remove the valve removal plug, pressure (approximately 300 PSI) released and struck him, blowing him 20 to 30 feet away. He was hospitalized.

An employee was driving a cement truck to the company's yard when he stopped the vehicle to inspect his load. While he was inspecting the load, the lid for the control panel closed unexpectedly and lacerated his left middle finger. He was hospitalized and had surgery.

Employees were using an air hoist to lift/move a crossover sub (pipe) on the platform floor. The lifting cap on the air hoist failed and the load fell on an employee's hand, causing a burst wound in his palm and a fracture in the bottom bone of his hand.

An employee and a coworker were simultaneously pouring two 5-gallon buckets of 34% hydrogen peroxide and a catalyst down a floor drain when a violent chemical reaction occurred, exposing them to gases and corrosive liquid chemicals. The employee was hospitalized with first and second degree burns to the face, neck, and arms.
An employee was removing a rigid metal flow line from a parts basket when the flow line shifted and fell on the employee's right leg, breaking the tibia and fibula.

An employee was preparing to shoot a fluid level on a well. He screwed an echo gun onto the well casing and opened the casing valve. When the pressure hit the gun, the outside of the casing valve threads failed and the pressure popped, releasing H2S (hydrogen sulfide) gas into the employee's face.
An employee was changing a polished rod when the employee's hand was caught between a well head and a block, crushing the ring and pinky fingers.
An employee was tapping on the valve. A 3-inch valve fell off the load line and struck the employee's right shin resulting in a broken lower leg.

An employee was using a 24-inch pipe wrench to make up a connection on a sinker bar, which was on stands on the ground, when he lost his footing and slipped. His lower right leg became twisted and suffered a spiral fracture.
An employee was found unresponsive inside of a trailer with a running generator. He was hospitalized for carbon monoxide exposure.

An employee was rigging up a building top-drive track and had the drive track hoisted when he saw something in the pin hole. As he attempted to remove the object, his right index fingertip was caught and amputated in the pin hole.

Employees were repairing a headache rack for a pickup truck. The headache rack was taken off the truck and placed on jack stands; however, the headache rack was not level. The employees attempted to level the headache rack by placing another jack stand under the rack. As the jack stand was being placed under the headache rack, the rack fell off the jack stands. An employee was on top of the headache as it was being leveled. The employee fell off the rack and landed on wooden pallets that were next to the rack. The employee suffered a back injury and was admitted to the hospital.

An employee was loading/unloading a truck when the vehicle rolled off the road and down a hill. The employee's legs were pinned underneath the truck. The parking brake and wheel chocks were not used at the time of the incident.

A crew of three employees had just repaired a heater/treater water leg 3" vitriolic coupling and had pressured it up with a pump. A leak appeared at a bolt on the unit and the two injured employees proceeded to tighten it. While the two were tightening the bolt, they heard a pop and something gave away. They were drenched with liquid and gas. The third employee saw this and shut the pump down and was going to isolate the unit when it caught fire near the coupling. The fire spread to the two drenched employees. One employee suffered third degree burns while the second employee suffered second degree burns.

Employees were using an air hoist to remove the cover from a rotary transmission when the cover became stuck on a 5-gallon bucket. As an employee attempted to push the cover free from the bucket, the cover fell on top of his right arm. His right arm was trapped between the bucket and cover, crushing tissue and muscles. He then fell and fractured a bone in his left hand.
An employee was cleaning a H2S (hydrogen sulfide) tower using a H2O2 (hydrogen peroxide) chemical when a chemical explosion occurred. The employee suffered burns to an ear and leg.
An employee was installing a cooling tower over a pit when he fell approximately 12 feet into the pit, suffering bruising. Fall protection was not worn at the time.

An employee was walking on the beam portion of the pumping unit attempting to guide the "horse's head" into position when the "horses-head" moved unexpectedly and struck the employee's right foot resulting in a fracture and laceration to the foot.
An employee was slipping new drilling line when his right hand got caught in the sheave resulting in the amputation of four fingers. The thumb was not affected.

An employee was cleaning the inside of tank with a pressure washer and contacted his left foot with the pressurized water blast. It cut through the top of his safety shoe and caused a one inch cut to the left foot behind the big toe area. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was repairing wires going to the head switch and grabbed hold of a live wire resulting in electrical burns to both hands.

An employee was conducting well maintenance when the flow line (two inch steel pipe) snapped and struck the employee in the head, back and pelvic areas. The employee then fell approximately three feet sustaining a head laceration. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was assisting in rigging up and rigging down when their left hand was caught between the blow out preventer (BOP) and elevators. The employee sustained lacerations, contusions and fractures to their hand.
While performing pump maintenance an employee's right hand was caught in the pump area and crushed.

An employee was digging a hole in the ground using a high pressure vacuum truck while standing on the edge of the hole. As he was digging, his foot slipped under the stream causing an injection wound to his left foot that resulted in the amputation of a toe on the left foot.

An employee was cleaning the rig when he reached for something and fell 8 to 10 feet to the ground, fracturing ribs and puncturing a lung. He was hospitalized. His safety lanyard was unhooked at the time of the incident.
An employee was throwing scrap iron into a bin when a piece of scrap iron became caught on his left ring finger, partially amputating the distal tip.
An employee was exiting the "dog house" when his right pinky finger was caught and amputated between the door and the doorway.

An employee was loading equipment from a forklift onto the bed of a pick-up truck. When he attempted to step backward, his foot became caught on an object and he began to fall. He tried to catch himself by reaching to the ground and broke his left arm.
An employee was gauging a chemical transport tank when a hatch fell on and amputated his finger.

An employee was trying to enter the cab of an 18-wheeler by reaching for the steering wheel to pull himself up when he slipped and fell to the ground, fracturing his left fibula and tibia. He was hospitalized.

An employee was trying to run a sand line down a hole when the line stopped. The stopping motion threw a loop in the line. When the employee attempted to grab the line, it dropped down the hole and amputated three of his right-hand fingers.

An employee was shutting off the valve of a truck tank hose when the pressure caused the lid to blow off. The oil inside the tank then struck the employee, fracturing his pelvis and right wrist and causing a road rash on his chest area. He was hospitalized.
An employee was helping to install section pipe when the employee's right middle finger was caught and pinched between the flanges of pipe and the existing line.
An employee was adjusting the position of a mud tank during a rig-up when the tank's hook released and struck him. He suffered a chipped tooth and facial fracture.
An employee was testing a hydraulic catwalk when a 1-inch hydraulic line burst, causing high-pressure hydraulic fluid to release and lacerate the employee's left palm.

An employee was performing prime-up operations when a discharge hose with a winged connection came loose from a manifold trailer. Boost pressure was being applied to the hose, causing it to whip around and spray water. As the hose was whipping around, it struck and fractured the employee's lower left leg.
An employee was burned and hospitalized after a fire occurred at a natural gas well.
An employee suffered broken ribs when caught between the bottom part of the rig basket and the pump jack beam.

An employee was removing a two inch plug and was thrown by the pressure build up (1100-1200 psi). The employee suffered a puncture wound to the leg, a broken left arm and fractures to the head and face.

On February 19, 2017, an employee slid down a containment mat and struck a pressure gauge on the wellhead while attempting to pull slack in a wire line. He suffered a rib injury that required hospitalization.
An employee was leaving the dock area in the dark and walked into a steel park stop used as a bumper for trucks. Both shins were lacerate and the employee was hospitalized.
An employee loosening nuts using a hydraulic torque wrench pinched his left ring finger between the nut and wrench. The finger was amputated up to the first knuckle.
An employee was driving a tanker uphill when the truck started rolling back down the hill and jack-knifed. The tanker rolled over, and the employee suffered a concussion and internal injuries.
An employee was helping a coworker hook up a power swivel on a servicing rig when he slipped and fell between the rig and the rig floor, injuring his head.
An employee was descending the stairs of a drilling rig to take his break when he slipped and fell, suffering bruising.

An employee was pressure washing rig equipment. As the employee was removing the guard to trouble shoot the pressure washer, his gloved hand was pulled into the pulley and belt system resulting in a partial amputation to the right ring and middle fingers.

On 3/3/17, two employees were lighting the Stabilizer Reboiler Heater (21-H-205). An internal vapor ignition impacted the heater integrity and both employees that were in the process of lighting the heater were injured. One of the employees was admitted to the hospital for further treatment of burns to the face.

An employee was transferring product from a top tote tank to the bottom tote tank when the leg of the top tote tank shifted causing the top tote tank to pinch the employee's right thumb between the top tote tank and the bottom tote tank spark arrestor. The employee suffered a partial amputation to his right thumb.

The employee was sitting on a pumping unit walking beam trying to attach the horsehead. The horsehead struck the employee causing him to fall over 9 feet onto the lower portion of the pumping unit resulting in a fractured pelvis and fractured facial bones.
An employee was disassembling a manifold and a counter weight fell and struck his hard hat. The employee was hospitalized for a skull fracture, lacerations and a fractured rib.

An employee was changing an auger bit on a drilling rig when the employee noticed the pin hole was filled with dirt. The employee used his right middle finger to clear the hole when the Kelly bar moved and amputated his finger.

An employee was attempting to load a piece of 3" iron pipe onto a forklift to load it onto a trailer when the employee stepped backwards and tripped on containment, dropping the pipe, fracturing the left tibia.

A drilling rig was tripping out of the well. The derrick employee was moving the top of a pipe stand to the racking fingers when the employee's retractable lanyard line was caught by the descending top drive and he was pulled to his knees on the derrick platform. The employee sustained a left knee fracture and vascular damage to the left thigh.
An employee amputated two fingers when casing loosened from a retention nut, fell and struck the employee.

An employee was using a rig elevator to pull rods out of a hole. As he lowered blocks down the elevator, the block brakes failed, allowing the elevators to strike and fracture the upper phalange on his left thumb.

An employee was helping a coworker adjust the placement of a cellar cover when he slipped and his right middle fingertip was caught and amputated between the cellar cover handle and the matting board.

An employee was conducting a pressure test inside a wellhead to check for leaks. When he removed his pressure detecting equipment, excess air pressure was released and struck the employee's hand and face. The employee suffered a facial laceration and a laceration and fracture to his hand. The employee was wearing PPE at the time.
Employees were servicing a well. When the injured employee lifted tubing, his finger was caught between the slip segments and the well head resulting in amputation of the middle fingertip.
An employee stepped off of the back of a trailer and placed his foot on the bumper. His foot slipped and was caught between the bumper and the trailer resulting in a fracture.

An employee was attempting to position a pipe on the swage unit using an F wrench style tool. When the employee was applying force to the tool, it slipped off of the pipe and the employee struck his hand on the metal table runner. The employee's hand was pinched between the tool and the table runner resulting in partial amputation of the right middle finger.

The injured employee was assisting another employee to remove a joint of drill pipe from the pipe rack/gull wings by utilizing an extended boom forklift. The rack was in close proximity to the motor sheds. In order to reach the joint of drill pipe, the forklift was positioned at a 45 degree angle from the rack. The injured employee used lifting slings to raise the load and was caught between the motor shed and the joint of drill pipe injuring his right leg.
An employee was nippling up a blowout preventer when the cable holding a flange broke and the flange fell onto the employee's left hand, amputating the left index finger distal phalanges.
An employee was blowing down a compressor when he fell down and suffered facial fractures, requiring hospitalization.
An employee was flowing production water to his water trailer when he tripped over a pipe at the well site and fell on his face. He broke his nose and required hospitalization.
An employee was offloading perforating guns from a trailer to the ground when his fingertip was pinched between two sections of pipe, resulting in an amputation.
An employee was struck by a pipe while attempting to open a bleed line, suffering contusions and broken bones in his torso. He was hospitalized.

An employee had changed the packing on a frac pump and was preparing to install the plunger when the plunger slipped and smashed his finger against the corner of the fluid end, amputating a portion of his left pinky.
An employee was using a high-pressure water line when the water punctured the skin on his leg. His wound became infected and required hospitalization.
An employee was removing a 4" valve with a flange. As he was removing the valve, his right pinky finger was caught between the flange of the valve and the pad-I, amputating it at the first joint.
An employee was moving equipment from a stand to the ground when his right middle fingertip was pinched and amputated between the equipment and the stand.
An employee was changing a light bulb when the globe around the bulb broke. The broken glass then amputated his fingertip.
An employee finished loading a trailer and exited the trailer via the trailer stairs. The employee slipped on the stairs and fell breaking her left wrist. The employee was hospitalized for surgery.

An employee was cutting a fallen tree that was laying on a telephone cable. When the tree was cut, pressure was released on the telephone cable, which sprung back up and threw the limb toward the employee. He suffered a contusion to the right side of his face.
An employee was performing rig-down operations for an oil drilling rig when a large cylinder fell and crushed the employee's right leg below the knee resulting in amputation.
An employee was trying to get sand to flow through a slot gate when it closed and amputated two of the employee's fingertips.

An employee was performing maintenance on a setting tool used in hydraulic fracturing. He opened a vise and turned the tool 180 degrees to make it easier to service. As he was sliding the tool back into the vise, the tool fell and caught his finger between the tool and the vise, amputating his left middle finger below the nailbed.
On April 5, 2017, an employee was disassembling a setting tool when the employee's right third finger was caught in the tool, partially amputating the fingertip.

On April 6, 2017, at approximately 3:10 p.m., an employee was spotting for a driver who was backing a 3/4 ton truck up to a trailer. The doors to the trailer were open for loading. Using the driver's side mirror, the driver backed toward the trailer. As the truck approached the trailer, the wind caused the door to the trailer to close. The employee moved between the truck and trailer to open the trailer door when his leg was pinched between the truck receiver and trailer bumper. He suffered a contusion to the left calf muscle.

An employee was at a gas extraction facility cleaning a knock-out vessel. As the employee was pumping down the knock-out vessel, a fire ball from the flare backed up through the 4-inch line that was connected to the knock-out vessel and burned the employee's left hand, torso, and back.
An employee was working inside the shop when a propane leak caused an explosion. The employee suffered third degree burns.

An employee was moving a truck and trailer when the trailer jack-knifed. A second employee was assisting the first employee with the trailer. The injured employee was standing next to the trailer directing the truck driver, when the trailer rolled over on top of him resulting in broken legs.
An employee was struck by the raised fork of a forklift, losing an eye.
An employee fell from a ladder and fractured an arm and a leg.

An employee was power-washing the rig. He shut it off to address an issue with some equipment and returned to relieve the pressure in the washer. He had his hand out when residual pressure in the washer line caused the water to release and cut through his glove and into his right hand, requiring hospitalization.
An employee was adjusting a rathole ring clamp. The ring clamp slipped off the rathole and the employee lost his balance and fell into the cellar resulting in a broken ankle.
An employee was using a chain to winch an object when the chain snapped and a tow cable smashed through the window and broke the employee's right arm.

An employee was working on the rig floor installing a lift cap into a mud tool. As the driller came up with the elevators his right middle finger was caught in between the elevators and the lift cap, partially amputating his finger.

An employee was checking water lines for leaks. When he found a leak, the employee applied a pincher device that crushes the line to stop the flow of water. A clamp on the device popped off and struck the employee on the chin fracturing four teeth on his lower jaw.

While an employee descended a wooden stair case, a stair tread began to give way. The employee shifted his weight to the handrail and the handrail gave way, causing the employee to fall approximately two feet to the ground. The employee landed on his back, then slid down the hill and contacted a concrete barrier. The employee was hospitalized with lower back pain.
An employee was struck on the left side by a cable coming from the cable drive while drilling.

Employees were tripping pipe out of the hole. An employee wanted to roll a pipe section from the catwalk onto the skate. The pipe was having difficulty rolling, so the employee changed the angle of the catwalk. The employee operating the catwalk lowered the catwalk on one corner using the hydraulic to level it out. The employee who was rolling the pipe got his foot crushed underneath the corner of the catwalk when it was lowered.

Employees were depressurizing a level bridle when the hose between the bridle and the flare system broke releasing hydrofluoric acid (HF). The two employees were exposed to the chemical vapor resulting in injury to their eyes, facial skin and lungs. Both employees were hospitalized.
An employee was changing slips on a rig when his hand became caught in the machine parts, resulting in amputation of part of his finger.
An employee was unscrewing the oil and gas pipe and was pushed over the edge of the work floor by the high pressure release. The employee fell 10 feet to the ground and broke his left arm.
While loading water from a pipeline into a trailer, an employee was struck by a pipeline pig that ejected out of the pipeline. The employee suffered a broken ankle and leg.

An employee had entered a confined space in a reactor when he slipped on catalyst support media. As he fell, catalyst support beams (fire brick stacks) weighing approximately 80 to 100 pounds also fell and struck his legs, fracturing his right ankle, right fibula, and left fibula.
An employee was inspecting an excavation on his knees. When he tried to stand up, he slipped and fell 8 feet into the excavation, hitting his head on a pipe. He was hospitalized with a head injury.
An employee was closing a cantilever pipe gate when the employee's left ring finger was crushed and amputated between the gate and the cradle it sits in when closed.

An employee was unloading salt water from the truck-mounted storage tank. As the employee removed the pressurized tank cap, it struck him on the right side of his torso resulting in injuries to his ribs and liver (right side).

An employee was clearing the pump to get the turbine ready for maintenance. While flushing the heavy coker gas oil (HCGO) pump, some HCGO got reintroduced into the pipe. When the hot oil (700 degrees) touched the water in the sewer drain, it flashed back and burned the employee. The employee suffered second degree burns to the abdomen and third degree burns to both hands and knees.
An employee was laying down pipe. His left hand was on the pipe elevator. When the elevator opened, it pinched his left ring finger. His left ring fingertip had to be surgically amputated.
An employee was attempting to attach a winch line onto a chute. As the line was being hoisted, the hook assembly amputated his right ring finger to the first knuckle.
An employee was struck in the shoulder by a casing pipe during a well completion operation. The employee then suffered a reaction to painkillers.

An employee was testing the flow of oil and gas at a job site. When he shut off the light plant (generator), a spark occurred and ignited gas that was in the air. The gas tank exploded and the flames burned 30 percent of his body.

While climbing a ladder to an acid gas/ammonia gas drum platform, an employee missed the second rung from the top of the ladder and fell approximately 7 feet. The employee suffered a fractured hip and lacerated elbow.

An employee was running rods in a hole when the rod transfer cable failed, allowing the rod to move uncontrollably. It struck the employee on the left side of the neck and cranium. He lost consciousness and suffered blood clots, requiring hospitalization.
An employee was participating in a flow back operation when a sand separator tipped and fell onto the employee. The employee was hospitalized with a broken femur and a broken hip.
While using a tag line to move a pipe, an employee lost control of the tag line. The employee's right arm was then caught between the pipe and a drilling rig, breaking it.
An employee was helping a coworker with a kelly belt when a 48-inch steel pipe wrench kicked back and struck the employee, fracturing the employee's left forearm.

A well-servicing rig crew was tripping pipe out of a hole when the safety pin on the tongs (torqueing device) broke, allowing the tongs to strike an employee and knock him off the work platform. He fell 10 feet, fracturing his ribs and back and lacerated his liver.

An employee was exiting the cab of a bulldozer. The employee slipped on the track while stepping down. The employee's lower left leg became lodged between the track and the bulldozer's blade, fracturing the tibia, fibula, and patella. The employee was hospitalized for surgery.

An employee was retrieving a wrench from his company truck. A water hauler truck (18 wheeler) reversed into the employee's pick-up truck. The employee's leg was caught in the door jam as he jumped into the truck resulting in a lower leg fracture.
An employee was spotting for a tractor and trailer when he became trapped between the trailer and a piece of stationary equipment. His pelvis was crushed and he required hospitalization.

An employee was helping to rig down a rig floor when the floor plate became hung up and slid out, striking him in the hard hat. He suffered a laceration on the right side of his forehead, requiring surgery, and fractures to his fifth and seventh vertebrae.

An employee was doing maintenance on a hydraulic tong. He was using his left index finger to remove water from the top of the tong's ring gear when the machine was activated. The tong began to rotate and pinched his left index finger, partially amputating it.

Employees were changing weights on a work-over rig from a 12 o'clock to 6 o'clock position when one of the moving weights struck an employee in the back. He suffered broken ribs and a collapsed lung, requiring hospitalization.
An employee's hand was crushed between a slip joint and a tubing stack that was being raised out of a well head. Two of the employee's fingers had to be surgically amputated.

An employee was removing a threaded grease fitting from a valve. As the fitting came loose, it struck the employee's hand. Air, water, and grease also released with some pressure. The pressure or the fitting lacerated the employee's hand between the thumb and forefinger and abraded the skin between the thumb and wrist. The employee was hospitalized and had surgery.
An employee was helping to trip tubing out of a well hole while working on the rig floor when his index fingertip was crushed between pipe tubing and the rig elevator.
An employee was opening the oil tank hatch when a spark ignited the material inside the tank. The employee sustained burns to the face, back and hands.
An employee was changing a well pump and attaching the pump jack head when the pump jack amputated the last digit of the employee's right ring finger.

An employee was stabbing a valve on a stack while guiding a forklift operator who was lifting and holding the rigged valve. The strap slipped off the valve, allowing the valve to fall and strike the employee's lower left leg, breaking it.

On May 24, 2017, at approximately 9:00 p.m., an employee was attempting to isolate a pump and needed to clean the strainer basket. After opening the system, the employee was hit with steam, suffering second degree burns and requiring hospitalization.
An employee became dehydrated while working on a rig and doghouse, requiring hospitalization.
An employee was welding outside when he experienced leg and arm cramps. He was hospitalized due to heat stress and dehydration.
An employee opened the gasoline cap to a utility trailer's generator when a flash fire occurred, causing first and second degree burns to the employee's face and hands.

An employee and a coworker were attempting to loosen rusted bolts using a wrench and a sledgehammer. The employee was holding the wrench while the coworker struck the bolts with the sledgehammer. As the employee began to stand up, his coworker struck him with the sledgehammer, breaking his left middle finger.
An employee was helping to install an orbit valve when his right ring fingertip was caught and partially amputated between the orbit valve and a flowline flange.
An employee was cleaning the threads on a 6-inch hammer union when he lacerated his right middle finger, requiring stitches. The laceration was infected and required hospitalization.
An employee was breaking down an oil saver assembly when his left index finger was smashed between two end joints of tubing, requiring surgery.
An employee was climbing a stationary ladder when he fell and landed on his back.
An employee was breaking out a stand of drill pipe when the pipe fell on and amputated two of his toes.

On June 1, 2017, at approximately 4:00 a.m., an employee was about to perform maintenance on an oil and gas down-hole mechanical setting tool. The employee picked up the 70 lb. setting tool to bump it on the ground and release the pressure. The tool was slippery from being covered with honey oil, and the employee's grip slipped. His right middle finger was then crushed and amputated by the setting tool.
An employee's left ring and pinky fingers were smashed between the top of a tank and a handrail on a gas buster tank. His left ring finger was partially amputated.

An employee was exposed to hydrochloric acid vapors while hooking up hoses to pump chemicals. The employee became dizzy and required hospitalization. Proper PPE was not worn at the time of the incident.
An employee was using a setting tool to compress a tube when his left middle fingertip was amputated.
An employee was performing maintenance on equipment while pressuring the unit up to the correct PSI. His hand was on top of the equipment when the air punctured his hand.
An employee was latching tubing with elevators at a rig when his left index finger was caught and smashed between the tubing collar and the handle on the elevator. He was hospitalized.
An employee was checking a valve on a blowout preventer when the position ram amputated his right pinky finger.

An employee was trying to remove sand that was stuck in a jammed sand equipment door. The employee was using a hammer on the door when the door slipped and caught the employee's left hand, crushing the index, middle, and ring fingers.

An employee was rigging up a crane when the employee's right pinky finger was caught in a pinch point between the outrigger cylinder and the outrigger beam, amputating it from the center knuckle and below.
An employee was moving a crane pad and amputated the right pinky finger at the first knuckle when it was caught in a pinch point between the outrigger and the cylinder.

An employee was opening the first of two plug valves on a blow-down line when a threaded nipple on the de-sander dislodged, causing the iron with the plug valves to strike him. He suffered a 2-inch laceration to the left knee, a small face laceration, a torn MCL in the right knee, and right shoulder tenderness.

An employee was tripping steel rods out when a string of the steel rods fell from their vertical position. He was running from the falling rods when his left leg was caught and injured on a cement pad and hardline.
An employee lost his balance while working on an elevated surface that was approximately 24 inches from the ground, fell and broke his arm.

On June 14, 2017, an employee was oiling the thumb of an excavator when the employee's hand became trapped between the excavator's bucket and thumb. The employee suffered left hand fractures and lacerations, requiring hospitalization.

An employee was cutting 3/4-inch strips of wood with a table saw when a piece of scrap wood became stuck between the guard and the saw blade. As the employee attempted to remove it, the left index fingertip contacted the blade and was partially amputated.
An employee was rolling pipe when he became fatigued due to heat exhaustion.
An employee was unpinning a stand pipe to reposition it when his knee was trapped between the stand pipe and a substructure, causing soft tissue damage.
An employee was exposed to hydrochloric acid vapors while operating a blender.
An employee was working on a pump when the brake was released and the plunger smashed his left wrist and first knuckles.
An employee was loading pipes onto a trailer when his left hand was caught between a pipe and the trailer, injuring his thumb and his index and middle fingers.
An employee was rigging some 2-inch manifold piping near a well head when some of the piping tipped and struck the employee's lower left leg, causing a compound fracture.
An employee passed out while working on an oil and gas rig due to a combination of heat stress, dehydration, and blood sugar issues.
An employee was bitten on the right calf by a spider while working at a drilling rig.
An employee was bitten by a copperhead snake on the right index finger.
An employee was loading valves onto a lowboy trailer. When he stepped off the trailer, he tripped and fell to the ground, fracturing his right elbow and requiring overnight hospitalization.

An employee was attaching the rigging on a base weight when his left foot was caught in the chains. The chains then pulled tight and trapped his left foot between the chains and the hitch, amputating his left big toe.

On June 30, 2017, an employee was operating a snubbing unit, getting ready to pull pipe out of a well, when a 2-inch hose popped off and struck him, fracturing his right forearm and requiring surgery.
An employee was using a saw to build pallets when the blade lacerated the employee's left hand.

An employee was rolling pipes by hand on top of the first layer of pipes in the pipe rack, when he lost balance and his right foot was caught between the pipes from the first layer. As he tried to stop an incoming rolling pipe with his left foot, he fell on top of the pipes and fractured his left ankle and a little bone in the leg. He was hospitalized.
An employee was trying to install a rotating head when his right thumb was caught and amputated between the rotating head and a drill pipe.

An employee was rigging down casing tools. He had two rig bales on the rig floor and was readying them to be let down to the rig floor. He had one bale upright when the rig-hand helper picked up the other bale and caught his ring finger between the two, partially amputating his distal fingertip.
An employee was adjusting a dump table gear on a piece of work when a coworker who was helping energized the equipment. The rotating equipment then amputated the employee's pinky fingertip.

A workover crew was tripping out of a hole when the drill line parted, causing the blocks to drop from 10 to 15 feet up and fall onto the floor. The drill floor sprung up when the blocks contacted it, throwing an employee off the floor. He fell approximately 15 feet onto the ground, breaking a rib.
On July 3, 2017, an employee was installing PVC pipe and using a chop saw when the employee experienced heat stress and heat exhaustion symptoms. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was lifting a drive shaft from a pump using chains when one of the chains came off and struck the employee's right leg, lacerating and dislocating the right knee.
An employee was lifting a perforated gun string to go down in a hole when the gun string broke loose and struck the employee's lower back, breaking the tailbone.

An employee was picking up a trip nipple with a hoist when the hoist became hung on top of a drive. The employee used the left hand to free the hoist. Once the hoist was freed, the trip nipple sprung up and caught the employee's left hand between the nipple and the elevator, breaking it.

An employee was acting as a ground guide as a pickup truck was laying out a hose. The hose reel was not secured to the pickup truck bed and fell on the employee, injuring the left side of the employee's body and breaking the left ribs.
An employee experienced heat stress while performing pump maintenance, requiring hospitalization.

An employee climbed the steps of a work platform to inspect the passenger side of a pump trailer that was leaking. As he was descending from the platform, he slipped and fell into a sitting position on top of a bracket that went through his coveralls and punctured the inside of his right thigh.
An employee was using a hose to empty flowback water tanks at a drilling rig. When he removed the hose from the tank, he was sprayed with hot flowback water, which burned his arms and torso.
An employee was putting a stopper in the bottom of a glass tube. The glass tube broke and cut both of the employee's hands, amputating the left pinky fingertip.

An employee was helping to remove a drill pipe from a hole. His right hand was on the stand of drill pipe while an iron roughneck operator retracted the equipment so it could be positioned out of the way. The iron roughneck operator swung the piece of equipment and struck the employee's right ring fingertip, amputating it.
An employee was holding some rigging when it moved, catching his hand and amputating a fingertip between the rigging and a pipe.

An employee was greasing valves when he dropped the grease hose. As he was reaching to stop the hose from hitting the ground, the handle struck the ground and was engaged, shooting grease up into his eye.
An employee was performing maintenance on a hot oil unit when his right pinky fingertip was caught and amputated on the pump.
An employee was attempting to remove a connecting collar using a wrench. The wrench slipped and he fell off the trailer, landing on the ground. He broke his hand and pelvis.
An employee was unloading pipe racks and drill collars when one pipe rack hit the other pipe rack, causing the load to shift and strike his lower leg. His lower leg broke and had to be amputated.
While rigging down after working for 12 hours, an employee began feeling weak and displaying signs of heat exhaustion. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was directing as 4-foot section I-beams were being loaded onto a flatbed truck when a beam fell from the truck and struck his right arm before landing on and breaking his right foot.
A door closed on an employee's little finger, amputating the terminal end.
An employee used tongs to pull a pipe apart and was trying to remove them from the pipe when the tongs struck and broke his ribs.

An employee was helping a coworker lower a cutting trough. The coworker attached a chain to the cutting trough and a shaker walkway overhang. The employee centered a forklift on the cutting trough and raised the forks up until they came into contact with the trough, to relieve any pressure from the saddle supports underneath. He un-pinned and removed one saddle support, then attempted to un-pin/remove the second support. He took his left hand and held the tubing and the slide portion of the saddle support in order to gain additional leverage to free the stuck pin. Once the pin came out, the slide fell and smashed his left index finger between the saddle and the tubing.
On 07/18/2017, an employee was working on a firewall when he began experiencing symptoms of heat stress, including nausea and vomiting. He was hospitalized for heat exhaustion.

An employee was trying to lower a tower on a light plant when the cable came out of the pulley and created slack. As the employee tried to put the cable back in the pulley, the cable snagged the employee's glove and pulled it into the pulley, amputating the first digit of the employee's right pinky finger.
While tripping in the hole, an employee stepped on a rotary table to grab a stand of drill pipe. His left leg went out from underneath him and he fell, fracturing his right tibia and fibula.
An employee was moving pipes on an oil rig and became sick to his stomach and vomited. The employee suffered a heat-related illness.
An employee was changing the swabbing cup on a workover rig when a pipe slipped down approximately 12 inches and amputated the employee's index and middle fingers at the middle joint.
An employee was raising a derrick on an oil platform when the derrick came in contact with a high-voltage power line. The employee suffered electrical burns.

During disassembly of a spent perforating-gun tool string, an employee attempted to carry the setting tool (designed to set a plug in the well) section from the external stands into the trailer for breakdown. When he lifted the setting tool in the vertical position, he placed his right hand over and into the open end of the sleeve. At that point, the internal mandrel shifted further up to the open end. His right middle fingertip was pinched by the mandrel and the set-screw opening at the end of the sleeve, amputating the distal phalanx.
An employee was assisting in mobilizing a rig when his right thumb was smashed, fractured, and lacerated between two metal pieces weighing about 30 to 40 pounds each. He was hospitalized.
An employee was driving around a curve in the road when his truck left the roadway and rolled over. He suffered a fractured pelvis.

An employee was washing out a hydrovac truck at a dump site. While holding the high pressure hose, he was pushed back but his feet were stuck in the mud so he fell back and lost control of the high pressure hose. High pressure water shot through his right forearm.
An employee suffered a right middle finger amputation while working with a chain.
An employee was beginning to bolt up a section of pipe. The pipe fell, which resulted in the amputation of the left leg above the knee.
An employee was using hydraulic tongs to run pipe in a hole when the slips failed, causing the tongs to come down on the employee's right foot, fracturing it.
An employee was tripping pipe when his finger was caught and amputated between a set of power tongs and a pipe wrench.

On July 26, 2017, an employee drove a utility vehicle up a hill to refuel a water pump. While driving the vehicle off the hill, the employee ran into mud, at which time the vehicle's back end kicked out. As he was trying to stop the vehicle, he fractured his left tibia, requiring hospitalization.
An employee had been assisting with a pipe weld. During clean-up operations, he began experiencing muscle cramps and shortness of breath. He was hospitalized for heat-related illness.

An employee was injured during tear down of an oil rig to be transported and set up at a new drilling site. The employee removed a retaining pin that held the pole upright and the pole fell onto the employee's leg breaking the femur bone and requiring surgery and hospitalization.
An employee was in a manlift preparing to pressure wash a pump jack. When the pump jack lowered it struck the manlift basket. The employee suffered two broken toes on the left foot.

While rigging up the top drive, employees needed to move the Kelly hose into position. They had to swing the ST-80 all the way around. The injured employee was in a crush point, and his foot was caught while stepping out of the crush point. The ST-80 was pulled over, trapping the employee's body between the ST-80 and the derrick leg. The employee sustained three broken ribs, a lacerated liver, and a collapsed lung, all on the right side.
An employee was working with a high pressure pump replacing swab. When the cap plug was unscrewed it fell out onto the employee's right middle finger, breaking the finger.

An employee was using a sledgehammer to hit a piece of pipe. The hammer deflected and smashed his right pinky finger between the head of the hammer and the tubing tongs. The employee sustained a laceration and fracture to his right pinky finger resulting in hospitalization.

The employee was assisting with mobile rig removal from a well site. As pipe was being pulled from the hole, rope used for pullout got caught up and pipe began to slip. The employee reached in to grab the pipe and his hand/finger was caught between piping and the drilling equipment, resulting in amputation of the right middle finger down to the knuckle.

On August 3, 2017, at approximately 9:00 a.m., an employee was tending a well while standing between two gas production units approximately 15 feet from a sand separator. At that time, a threaded pipe that was going into the top of the sand separator blew apart. The pipe separated at a 90 degree elbow and released approximately 2,300 lbs. of pressure. The gas from the line projected down towards the ground and the employee's skin was struck by ground debris. He was hospitalized.
An employee was mixing caustic soda in a mixing barrel when it reacted and splashed on him, causing chemical burns to his right and left wrists, left bicep, and both knees.

An employee was attempting to remove a pin from a derrick when a forklift operator moved the derrick board unexpectedly. The employee's right thumb was then caught and amputated between the pin and the handrail.
An employee's left index finger was caught and crushed between an elevating latch and a pipe stump on a drilling rig, requiring amputation.
An employee was inspecting counter weight cylinders for clearance when the employee fell from the top of the counter weights to the crane deck, suffering a facial fracture.
An employee fell from an exchanger rig as he descended. The employee fell onto a basket made of angle iron and fractured ribs and bruised a lung.
An employee was unloading a truck tank when he was exposed to hydrogen sulfide, suffering a headache and nausea.

An employee was servicing an oil rig when a rod transfer became hung up, came loose, and struck the employee, knocking him out of a rod basket. He landed face first on a tubing board and broke his leg, jaw, nose, and other facial bones.
An employee was grinding a piece of metal plate to install it on a service truck when the grinding wheel came off and struck the employee's forearm just above the wrist, fracturing the ulna.
Two employees were performing servicing work at a natural gas refrigeration plant when a fire erupted and seriously burned their backs.
An employee was burned on their back from a gas-related fire.
A pole truck was lifting a piece of equipment when the chain failed and struck an employee on the head and shoulder. The employee suffered a head laceration.

An employee was adjusting the high/low switch on his truck-mounted welder. He was turning around when he lost his footing because it had just rained and his truck bed was slick. He went to steady himself and reached to grab onto something with his hands. His right hand slid underneath the cowling of his welder and two fingers were severely lacerated by the motor fan blades. He was hospitalized.

An employee was rigging down bales that were being lowered out a V door and down a slide with a winch. As the bales were being lowered to the catwalk via the slide, one section became stuck on a roller on the rig floor. When the employee reached down to free the bale, it came free and knocked him off balance. He fell through the V door and down the slide, striking an object and suffering fractured facial bones, broken ribs, and a collapsed lung.

An employee was guiding a section of fracturing iron (straight joint and checksum) as two coworkers were lowering the checksum out of the way. The injured employee's gloved right hand was caught between the straight joint and a wing for a suction hose. The straight joint rolled, allowing employee to pull his hand out of the glove. His right middle finger was fractured and lacerated, requiring amputation.

An employee was making a connection with tongs and cables when one of the cables on the (muffled) drive caught the tongs and lifted them up. He held on to the tongs for approximately 10 feet before he fell to the ground. He landed on his side, fracturing ribs and vertebrae and puncturing a lung. He was hospitalized.
An employee's right index and middle fingers were caught and amputated between model-C slips and annulars.

An employee was changing a saver sub, using a sling around a grabber box, when the rating tag on the sling was pinched under the grabber box. The employee was using a wrench to try and pry out the rating tag when the grabber box fell and caught the employee's fingers, amputating the first digit of the right middle finger.
While stepping out of a pickup truck to purchase gasoline, an employee slipped off the running board and fell to the ground. The employee dislocated an ankle and had surgery.

An employee was lowering a well pump down a well shaft when a 1/2-inch cable snapped and whipped back up, striking the employee. He suffered lacerations to both hands and bruising on the chest, requiring hospitalization.
An employee was working at a wellsite when his right little fingertip was amputated.
An employee was opening a high-pressure relief valve with a pressure bar. He was pulling down on the bar when it gave way, causing him to fall on the second bar. He tore his left triceps and bicep.

An employee was holding the wing side of a swivel connection in place to connect an iron riser to a wellhead when his right pinky finger was caught between the iron riser and the threaded part of the well, amputating it above the nail.
An employee was walking past a parked truck when four pipe joints fell off the truck and struck his back, fracturing it.

An employee was using a pressure washer to wash a drilling rig when the washer hose became twisted. As the employee was untwisting it, the pressure washer ran over his boots, causing hot water to burn his foot and debris to enter his left middle toe. He required surgery to remove the debris.

An employee was nippling up a blowout preventer at a drill site when the employee's hand was caught between a blind ram and 4-inch gauge sealer valve, crushing the right pinky finger. The employee's pinky finger was amputated.
An employee was attempting to replace a gasket in a valve on a separator trailer when he fell and struck a tire rim that was on the ground, breaking ribs and suffering spleen damage.

A drilling crew was in the process of tripping pipe out of a hole when the pulling cable snapped, letting the block fall freely on the rig floor. A piece of the cable hit one of the employees and became embedded in his right leg, requiring surgery and hospitalization.
An employee was tightening the fan belt on a large compressor when his right pinky fingertip was caught and amputated in the fan belt.
An employee was bitten on the neck by a black widow spider while carry a tool on his shoulder.
An employee was testing a 10,000 lb. frac valve. The quarter-inch needle valve came off and pressurized water shot through his left thigh.
An employee was laying down drill pipe when he felt body cramps and said he was going to pass out. The employee was hospitalized overnight for renal failure due to heat exposure.

An employee was traveling on a lease road making a left hand turn when the tractor trailer shut off completely causing power steering to no longer function. The tractor trailer left the roadway and rolled over onto the passenger side of the vehicle. The employee was admitted to the hospital and underwent surgery on vertebrae in the top region of the neck.
An employee was putting a tire on a vehicle when the jack slipped and struck his left wrist, causing six fractures.

An employee picked up a load of production water at a well site with his truck. As he was leaving the site, his truck's back tires left the roadway, causing the vehicle to roll over. He suffered four spinal fractures.

On September 16, 2017, at approximately 11:00 a.m., an employee and two vendor employees were repairing a tank dike liner with a heating iron. Flammable condensate leaked from the plumbing at a hammer union on ground level going to the condensate tank. The heat gun ignited the vapors resulting in third degree burns to the injured workers' hands and face. One employee was hospitalized.

An employee was stenciling pipe when he dropped the stencil. As he was picking up the stencil, he placed his left hand on the pipe rack and a pipe moved, catching his left ring finger between the pin stop and housing. The employee sustained a partial left ring finger amputation.

An employee was working on a palletizer, went to the back side of the machine, and was struck by/caught between the machine's ram and frame. The employee suffered broken ribs and other injuries. The machine's guard had been bypassed at the time of the incident.

An employee and driver were unloading a frac tank from a winch truck. While trying to unhook the winch cable from the tank, the driver tightened the winch cable instead of loosening it, pinching the employee's finger between the cable and rear roller. The employee's right index fingertip was amputated.
An employee was reaching down to pick up a flashlight that he dropped when a rattlesnake bit his finger.

An employee was using a forklift to move a bale, weighing approximately 1000 lbs., to a c-can for storage. When the employee unsecured the bale from the forklift, the bale fell off the forklift and onto the employee, fracturing his ankles.

An employee was getting pipe and weld data off a pipe that was being cut after hydrotesting when the pipe fell on the employee's legs, breaking two bones above the right ankle. The employee was hospitalized and had surgery.
An employee was setting drill pipe slips when his right foot slipped and was caught in the drill pipe slips, crushing the end of his foot. He was hospitalized overnight and had surgery.

Employees were running packers and had just finished a job. The injured employee was kneeling down on the left knee on the under floor (floor that was six feet off the ground) when a sudden burst of pressure and flow back struck the injured employee's right side dislocating an elbow, breaking the ulna and causing various abrasions and bruises.

A crew was attempting to hang a metal horse head on a pumpjack while the injured employee was sitting on a 12-inch beam (12 feet off ground). As the crew was lowering the head, it fell out of its saddle and smashed the employee's left arm, which became very swollen and possibly fractured.

An employee was attempting to latch an elevator on a turbine. The elevator did not latch properly and opened/came off the joint turbine. When the employee tried to re-align the turbine, his thumb was caught and fractured between the turbine and the elevator.
An employee sustained a snake bite on the left index finger.
An employee was conducting well-servicing operations when a hammer union came apart and fell, striking and lacerating the employee's head.
An employee was opening a valve while standing on the platform when the employee fell approximately 3.5 feet to the ground, breaking ribs.
An employee's left hand was caught by a pipeline that was being lowered by a rig, partially amputating his thumb, index finger, and forefinger up to the knuckle. He was hospitalized.

An employee was working on a rig site when a thunderstorm struck the area. Because of extremely high winds, the rig was shut down and everyone was told to go to the muster area. A trailer turned over on its side and struck an electrical line at the muster area, energizing the trailer. When the employee reached the muster point, he contacted the trailer and was electrocuted, requiring hospitalization.

An employee was rolling tubing from the pipe rack onto the pipe wrangler. The pipe rack was not flush with the wrangler due to the contour of the ground. The tubing came down while his hand was underneath the pipe rack and pinched his left ring finger resulting in a partial amputation.
An employee was working approximately 6 feet above ground level servicing a pumpjack when he lost his footing and fell to the ground, fracturing three ribs.

An employee was attempting to climb a ladder onto a trailer when he slipped, tried to catch himself, and placed his right hand between the ladder and the trailer. His weight caused the space between the ladder and the trailer to flatten, and his right pinky finger was caught and partially amputated between the ladder and trailer.

An employee was filling a tanker trailer with used oil that was being pumped from a larger stationary tank. He climbed the trailer-mounted ladder to open the dome hatch to check on the filling process. When he released one of the dome hatch cover clips, the lid was blown open from built-up pressure inside the tank. He was thrown from the ladder to the ground, hitting his head and neck and requiring hospitalization.
An employee was pulling protectors off of a casing when a forklift operator dropped pipes on a pipe rack. One pipe rolled over and smashed the employee's finger.
An employee was attempting to unplug an air compressor from a wall when the electrical socket was pulled out of the wall. As he attempted to remove the plug, he received an electrical shock.

The employee added a liquid drain cleaner to the casing check valve to remove scale build up. The employee opened the system and hit the hammer union between two ball valves to relieve pressure that caused residual chemical in the line to splash back onto the employee's face and body. The employee suffered chemical burns to the face and body.

An employee was holding a fixed centralizer while casing tongs were being used to join together casing when the centralizer slipped from his hand. As he attempted to grab it, his fingertip was caught and amputated in the casing tongs.
An employee received second degree burns from steam from the coker drum while performing housekeeping duties.
An employee was torch cutting a tank when residual fumes ignited burning the employee's abdomen.

An employee and coworkers were attempting to change out a leaking O-ring. They were using a 3-ton come-a-long to create a gap when the hook on the come-a-long broke, causing the gap to close and smash the employee's right and left thumbs.
An employee was helping to unstring a drill line when the drill line became hung up in the fast line. The drill line then came free, striking and lacerating the employee's right thigh.
An employee was loading a pallet into a truck when he slipped and tore his left patella tendon, requiring hospitalization.
An employee fell while installing safety clamps. During the fall, the employee's left pinky finger was caught and partially amputated between a safety clamp and a pipe.
An employee slipped and fell approximately 4 feet while he was descending the four-rung fixed ladder of a tractor trailer. He broke his leg and ankle and was hospitalized.
During rig-down operations, an employee's left hand was caught between a hydraulic torque wrench and a flange, amputating his thumb from the mid-knuckle to the tip.
An employee was getting an oil sample from a hoist on the rig floor. He turned a valve and the hoist activated, amputating his right index fingertip.
Two employees were moving a 500-pound valve set from a rack when the valve set slid off the rack and struck one of the employee's left foot, fracturing it.

An employee was cleaning near an orbit valve that had a new actuator. The actuator showed that the valve was open when it was actually closed, causing a release that broke the employee's left leg. He was hospitalized and had surgery.

Two employees were rigging up while a third employee was using a truck to light the worksite with headlights. When the third employee exited the truck to help them, the truck rolled down and pinned the two employees. One employee was hospitalized with a cracked pelvis.

An employee was helping to load a beam onto a truck. He was trying to take a wood block out from under the beam when it fell from the forks of a forklift and caught his right index finger, amputating it between the first and second knuckles.

An employee was rigging down an isolation tool on a crane truck when he slipped on wireline grease that was on the bed of the mobile crane truck and fell to the ground, fracturing his left wrist, right elbow, and right shoulder.
An employee was helping a second employee unload pipe when a piece of pipe became stuck. The employee was pushing on the pipe when it gave way and crushed his left index fingertip.

An employee was greasing valves when he lost his footing and fell backward on a fluid pumping trailer. While he was falling, his right leg was caught in a 6-inch gap between the bumper and trailer, breaking his right fibula and tibia.
An employee's right index finger was crushed by a rig floor during rig-down operations, resulting in a fingertip amputation.

On October 16, 2017, at approximately 3:30 PM, a cat-line was attached to a cable to raise up a rig floor. An employee was attempting to un-pin the floor to remove it when the cable snapped and the floor fell on the employee, striking him in the back and pinning him for approximately 10 seconds. He fractured his spine.
An employee was putting a well online with a wrench when the flow line blew up. The employee received lacerations to the right arm, and the left ankle was nearly amputated.

Two employees were tightening up a connection on a pump when the wrench slipped and caught one of the employee's fingers between the skid and the wrench. The employee's finger was severely lacerated, resulting in an amputation to the first knuckle.

An employee was pushing on a tree while putting on a wraparound when the lifting sup separated from the well head flange at the threads, allowing the flange to drop and crush the employee's right hand.

An employee was rigging up an I-beam with a jib attachment and a lifting hook on the bottom side. His left pinky finger was caught in a pinch point between the jib and the hook when the signal was given to move the I-beam, amputating his fingertip.

A crew was attempting to line up a catwalk with a vee-door. An employee's left hand was resting on the catwalk. The employee signaled the driller on the controls to move the catwalk. The vee-door, which was resting on the catwalk, then shook free and swung down, smashing the employee's left pinky finger.

An employee was part of a rig floor crew that was picking up 2-and-3/8-inch drill pipe to make a connection with a power swivel. The employee grabbed the pipe above the elevators. At that point, 1/4-inch sling cables wrapped around the pipe and the employee's fingers, partially amputating the right middle finger and fracturing the right ring finger.

An employee was using an electric band saw to cut wood skids (to be used as spacers between pipes before they are buried and backfilled) when his hand was caught under the saw, amputating his pinky fingertip.

An employee was lowering a blowout preventer (BOP) into position. He placed his hand on top of a stud on the BOP flange while the BOP was being lowered. The stud became hung up and bottomed out on the pipe ram body, smashing his left hand. His left middle finger and knuckle were crushed and required surgery. Impact gloves were worn at the time of the incident.
An employee was stepping down from a machine bulldozer when he missed a step and fell, fracturing his left leg and requiring hospitalization.
An employee was lighting a boiler when a propane flashback occurred, burning the employee.

An employee was hooking up equipment to torque test when he stepped onto a wing valve that was 2 feet off of the ground. The wing valve broke, causing him to fall onto the ground. He suffered broken ribs and lower back injuries that required hospitalization.
An employee fell approximately 40 inches to the ground while walking on a flatbed trailer and arranging a rack system, suffering broken shoulder bones.

An employee was attempting to stab a piece of pipe while tripping in a hole when a boom gate fell on the employee's left foot, fracturing a metatarsal. The boom gate was up and in motion at the time of the incident.
An employee was working at a shaker table to properly dispose of oil and gas drilling waste when a water pump created an arc flash that burned the employee's face.

Two employees from two different companies were using a manlift to set a valve on a wellhead. The rigging from the crane carrying the wellhead became bound with the well, causing it to kick. The valve then loosened from the carrying straps and fell 14 feet, hitting the manlift. The two employees were knocked out of the manlift and fell 9 feet to the ground. One employee suffered a broken leg and was hospitalized. The other employee suffered minor injuries.

An employee was emptying a self-tipping dumpster that was attached to the forks of a forklift. He tilted the forks forward to help facilitate the dumping of the dumpster. He then got out of the cab of the forklift, walked to the side of the forklift mast, and placed his left hand on the lower portion of the mast. He reached up with his right hand and disengaged the release lever on the back of the self-tipping dumpster, causing the dumpster to quickly shift forward. The resulting shift in weight of the dumpster caused the forklift forks to swing back into the mast, pinching the employee's ring finger between the forks and mast. The tip of his ring finger digit was amputated.

An employee was rigging a flow line on a crane when the pipe became stuck. The employee approached the flow line to check it when it unexpectedly came loose and struck him in the chest, breaking four ribs.

On October 27, 2017, at approximately 2:45 p.m., an employee was adjusting the forks of a lift. While holding onto the side of the forklift assembly, he boomed up and kicked the fork over with his foot. As the fork moved, it dropped into place, along with the bar that supports the forks. The employee's gloved finger was then pinched between the fork and fork assembly, amputating his right middle fingertip.
An employee was changing the heads of tongs. The rig operator lost control of the power swivel and it struck the employee's leg, breaking it.

A rig crew was tripping rod out of a hole. When the operations were complete, the derrick man removed the screw from the clevis that supports the safety transfer to clean it. The safety transfer then slipped from his hand and hit an employee that was standing on the rig floor on the head. The employee suffered a laceration and possible concussion.

An employee was getting ready to load a truck. He was behind the winch truck, pulling on the chain that goes to the winch, when the driver in the truck pulled the lever that moves the chain that goes to the winch. The chain and the tail roll of the trailer trapped the employee's finger causing a partial amputation of the right ring fingertip.

An employee was operating a slick line truck to pull production tools out of an existing well. He was in the cab and the truck was stationary, when one of the slick line cables snapped under tension. The cable shot back into the cab of the truck and lacerated an artery in the employee's neck.
Two employees were removing ball valves. When the employees began to install the gaskets, a flash fire occurred. One employee suffered burns to the face.
An employee was unwrapping a wire rope from a spool when the wire rope slipped and pinched his left middle fingertip between the rope and spool. His fingertip was amputated.
An employee was picking up trash when he stumbled into an unguarded pumping unit and was struck by the horse head, suffering pelvic, sternum, and rib fractures.
An employee was prepping a mast to be moved to platforms when his left middle and ring fingers were caught between the chain/hook and mast, amputating his fingertips.

An employee was standing on the ground near a pipe rack while other employees picked up a joint from a catwalk. The joint came off its cradle, rolling back onto the pipe rack and hitting the employee. He was pinned between two joints, suffering bleeding in his abdominal cavity.
An employee was up on a stairway opening valves on a wellhead when the stairs gave way. The employee suffered a broken left leg.
An employee was picking up a mud motor to trip in a hole when a plate fell off the top drive and struck the employee, causing a right index finger amputation.

Employees were performing pressure services, hydrostatic testing on a blowout preventer. When one of the employees attempted to loosen bolts on the wellhead spool, the hydraulic torque hammer wrench and wellhead spool struck the employee s left hand, partially amputating the index finger.

An employee was performing housekeeping when he went to pick up a plunger at a frac site. The plunger then slipped and amputated his middle fingertip. Impact gloves were not worn at the time of the incident.
An employee was hammering one end of a hose when the opposite end blew off under pressure, striking the employee and causing a laceration.

An employee was working removing a set of elevators at a gas well drill site when a second employee started a power swivel. The employee's left arm became entangled in the power swivel, breaking it and partially amputating the left ring finger. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was hoisting up into a rig derrick when his foot was caught between two braces, amputating his left big toe.

An employee was removing a flange from a client's oil/gas well with a hydraulic torque wrench. While the employee was placing the torque wrench on the nut, the employee's finger was in a pinch point between the torque wrench and nut. The employee then inadvertently stepped on the controller, which activated the torque wrench, amputating the employee's right index fingertip and nail.
An employee was installing a rotating head bearing when the bearing slipped and smashed the employee's right hand, breaking it.

An employee was sitting on a casing head valve to hold himself up while working in a cellar. He was holding onto a stud with his left hand for support. He was cutting approximately 14 inches off of the casing using a torch when the blowout preventer became off-center and shifted to the side. His left index, middle, and ring fingers were then caught and smashed between the stud and casing, requiring surgical amputation of two fingertips at the base of the nail and one fingertip at the first knuckle.

An employee was walking down vee-door stairs, using the railing hand method on the hand rails. He was almost to the bottom when the roller assembly shifted and struck his left hand against the handrail, fracturing his pinky finger.

An employee was watching a sub-winch cable run through sheaves to ensure that the cable was running smoothly when he noticed slack due to the cable coming off the sheave. He grabbed the cable with his left hand for balance and placed his right foot on the lower section of the cable to push it into the sheave. The cable then broke free into the sheave, consequently creating tension on the cable, which cut his right foot and three left-hand fingers. His three middle left-hand fingers were amputated, and his right foot was partially amputated.

An employee was repairing a metal platform that was supported by metal saw horses and jack stands. A metal shim was in place on the saw horse to level the platform. The employee noticed the shim had turned slightly, so he used a 4 lb. maul to tap the shim into its original position. The force of the strike caused the shim to dislodge, and the corner of the platform came down on the employee's index finger. The employee suffered an amputation.
During well-servicing operations, an employee was removing an on/off tool when it slipped. His finger was then caught and smashed between the tool.

An employee was working from a servicing rig platform while tripping out pipe. The pipe became unstable and swung over the edge of the servicing platform while the employee was holding onto it. The pipe pulled the employee from the platform, and he fell approximately 15 feet to the ground. He suffered lacerations and fractures to the eye socket, jaw, nasal bones, and one of his legs. The platform was unguarded at the time.
An employee tripped and fell while walking across a rig floor, suffering multiple fractures to the left elbow.

On 11/16/2017, an employee was attempting to clear a hydrate formation in a gas pipeline at a tank battery when flammable gases and vapors ignited, causing first and third degree burns to his face, the back of his head, his back, and his hands.
On 11/16/2017, two employees were attempting to clear a hydrate formation in a gas pipeline at a tank battery when flammable gases and vapors ignited, causing significant burns to both employees.

Employees were setting, aligning, and starting a compressor. The injured employee was attempting to diagnose a squeak heard while the compressor was running when his left hand entered the rotating area of the compressor, amputating his left thumb.
An employee was draining a plug catcher when the valve arm became loose, spun closed, and hit his right leg, fracturing it. He was hospitalized.

An employee was using a tool to install a thread protector on a tubular when the tool's lithium battery exploded in the non-mag tubular, sending up debris and chemicals that struck employees on the rig floor. An employee was hospitalized with face and wrist burns.
An employee was using a hydraulic torque tool to take measurements when the tool released pressure, amputating the employee's left ring fingertip.
An employee received steam burns while performing maintenance on a transmitter, requiring hospitalization.
An employee was tripping out pipes when a pipe swung and crushed his right arm between two hanging pipes. His arm broke.
An employee was trying to loosen a tool with a wrench when his finger was caught between the wrench and the object he was loosening, resulting in an amputation.

An employee was tightening bolts on a pump jack with an impact wrench and 18-inch crescent wrench when it slipped. While trying to grab the wrench, the employee's hand was slammed against the pump jack, severing the last two digits of the left pinky finger.
A crew had just installed a high volume separator in an oil field when a blowout occurred. One employee sustained head injuries and was hospitalized.

A crew was pulling a second string of tubing out of a hole and was warming up a collar to break the connection. A swivel operator was spinning the swivel when an employee placed a 36-inch pipe wrench on the top part of the swivel, then placed a cheater bar on the pipe wrench. The swivel continued to turn clockwise with the pipe wrench and cheater bar attached. The employee was still holding onto the cheater bar when it started turning. The employee was then pulled and thrown off the rig floor, suffering a broken clavicle, broken ribs, collapsed right lung, and broken back.

A cement crew had finished a surface cement job and was preparing to rig down the cement head and equipment. An employee was preparing to remove the cementing head and manifold from the casing. The drilling rig crew loosened the chain boomer and lifted the casing to remove the slips. When the rig operator lifted the casing, the hook on the chain boomer broke, striking the employee in the hard hat and knocking him to the rig floor. He hit his head on the floor, losing consciousness and suffering a head laceration.

An employee was securing a flat hose to a reel on a deployment vehicle when the hose rotated. The employee was then caught between the reel and the deployment vehicle, fracturing the skull, jaw, and cheekbones.
An employee was attempting to climb up an angle iron piece of a substructure when he slipped and fell backward 4 feet to the ground, suffering a spiral fracture to his right ankle.
An employee was positioning an iron roughneck when his left middle finger was pinched between the lift nubbin and the roughneck, amputating his fingertip.
Two employees were attempting to light a pilot light on an incinerator when the gases ignited and back-flashed on them. They sustained facial and hand burns.

An employee was removing a fitting from an accumulator. Pressure was still in the safety bottle at the time. When he got down to the final threads, the fitting blew off, striking him in the face and neck. He suffered a facial contusion, orbital fracture, eye hematoma, and eyelid and neck lacerations.

An employee was using his right hand to feed a piece of metal into an iron worker metal forming machine and his left hand to operate the foot pedal, which had been moved up to the work surface near the machine. His left hand then entered the vertical metal forming device and was compressed, fractured, and lacerated.

On 12/8/2017, at 4:00 p.m., employee #1 was on a truck containing racks of 25-foot sucker rods helping to offload the rods to employee #2, who was stationed on the ground.
