Employee #1 dropped his end of the sucker rod, which struck the ground. The impact caused a wave motion to propagate through the sucker rod, which then caused the end that employee #2 was holding to fling out of his hands in an upward motion, striking and lacerating his nose and forehead.

An employee was rigging down a top drive on a drilling rig when a slide that was connected to a torque tube came down on the employee's left hand, amputating the middle finger just above the middle knuckle.
An employee was operating a vacuum truck when the hose became disconnected and began spraying hot fluid. A fire and then explosion occurred, and the employee suffered serious burns.
An employee was maneuvering a mud bucket away from a rotary table area when his right little finger was smashed between the mud bucket frame and a mast leg, resulting in an amputation.
An employee was caught between the forks of a forklift and a building, suffering crushing injuries to the abdomen.

Two employees were spotting for a sand truck. The front spotter lost sight of the back spotter, who was then pinned between the truck and a sand silo. He suffered a hip injury and herniation, requiring hospitalization.

An employee was checking tags on rods and moving a rod clamp when a suitcase, which held the rods, slipped. The employee's left thumb/index and pinky fingers were caught and smashed between the clamp and bridle. The employee suffered amputations to half of the index finger and the pinky fingertip.
Three employees were lifting a piece of pipe when it fell. One employee tried to catch it, but it fell on his hand and smashed his pinky finger. He was hospitalized and had surgery.

An employee was removing a drill collar when his glove became caught on it. His left hand was then crushed between the drill collar and drill stump, injuring his ring finger and requiring hospitalization.

An employee was using an air hose to blow air through a waterline to a well when the hose came loose from the strap that secured it to the water pump. The end of the hose struck the employee's left shoulder area, fracturing his collarbone.

On 12/14/2017, an employee was using a water jet "gun" with hot water coming out at 3,000 psi to spray columns in a sand pit. The high-pressure water then cut his leg, causing an abrasion and requiring hospitalization.

An employee was rolling out liner to build a containment for a frac tank to sit in. Employees were pushing liner and using a skid steer when the employee slipped and the skid steer came up and caught the employee's ankle, fracturing it.
An employee was standing between an excavator and a cutting box when he was struck by the excavator arm, fracturing his left arm and ribs.
An employee was using a pry bar to loosen a stuffing box when the tip of the bar slipped and amputated the employee's fingertip.
An employee stepped into an area where hot condensate was present and sustained a condensate burn to the lower right leg.

An employee was riding a crew bus to a job site when the bus stopped. The crew exited the bus and was standing on the side of the road when a private vehicle struck employee. He suffered multiple blunt force trauma.
An employee was lowering a standpipe in an articulating lift when four of the employee's left-hand fingers were crushed between the rail of the lift and the pipe, requiring hospitalization.

A workover crew was making up their last joint of tubing when an equipment operator picked up the slips before the injured employee moved the tongs out of the way. The tongs then struck the employee in the head.
An employee was attempting to adjust a glycol wrap on a pipe when it shifted. High-pressure water then exited the pipe and struck the employee, knocking him to the ground and breaking his ulna.

An employee was loading a pig into a pig launcher and closing the end hatch on a vertical pipe. The hinged pig launcher hatch began to fall and the employee attempted to catch it with his right hand, which was crushed between the pipe flange and hatch. He suffered soft tissue damage to his right middle and ring fingers, requiring hospitalization.

An employee was working in a flow back trailer when a generator stopped working. The employee tried to restart it and a fire started, causing third degree burns to the employee's hands and second degree burns to the face.

An employee opened an access panel on a pipe rattler unit to adjust the pipe by hand. His right hand made contact with the pipe cleaning brush, which was still energized at the time, rubbing the skin on his hand away to the muscle layer.

An employee was shutting down a compressor unit using the shut-down button inside an electrical panel. When he pressed the button, the door blew back from pressure and struck him, knocking him off his feet into a trash bin. He then got up to fight a small fire that had developed in the electrical panel. He suffered broken ribs as well as facial and chest contusions.
An employee slipped in the mud and fractured an ankle.

Two employees were working on a forklift due to a belt issue. The injured employee was working on the belt when the other employee started the forklift. The belt and pulley in the forklift motor then amputated the injured employee's right index fingertip.

An employee was performing maintenance on a coil tubing unit, removing a bad section of coil from a reel. While trying to clear a jam in the large coil, the injured employee was struck by the coil, suffering a fractured ankle and elbow.
An employee slipped on ice and fractured an ankle.
An employee was operating a grader and then stopped to climb out. He lost his grip on the handle and fell to the ground, landing on his right shoulder. He fractured his right scapula and humerus.
An employee was trying to reduce the high liquid level on the site-glass when a compress exploded, causing second degree burns to 5 percent of the employee's body.
An employee was installing handrails on a scaffold when he fell approximately 10 feet to the ground. He was hospitalized with a fractured neck.
An employee was standing on a rig floor when equipment fell off a mast as it was erected and struck the employee, causing significant head and neck injuries. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was walking down a ramp and slipped on an icy surface, suffering a left leg fracture.

An employee was warming up a hydraulic cylinder with a propane heater when hydraulic fluid shot through a pinhole leak in the feed line toward the propane heater and ignited. The employee suffered burns to the face and hands.

An employee was getting ready to climb a ladder to a chemical float trailer. He had put his right hand on the lower section of the ladder when it shifted, causing his right ring finger to be caught between the ladder and the trailer. His fingertip was amputated.
An employee was changing out an expansion joint with another employee. While they were breaking the bolts loose, oil-based mud leaked out and burned his skin. He was hospitalized.

An employee was blowing off pressure on a field natural gas compressor when a pipe about 3 feet long pulled out of the threads and hit the employee, causing blunt force trauma to the face, arm, and shoulder.
An employee was guiding a third-party truck back into the yard to pick up product when he was pinned between the truck tire and a pallet of product, breaking his right tibia. He was hospitalized.
While pulling drilling rods, a driller did not stop and hit the crown of a derrick block. The rods then hit a derrickman, breaking his pelvis.

An employee was troubleshooting the natural gas supply for a freshwater heater. The employee opened a valve on a scrubber that released gas and it ignited, burning the employee's legs, hands, and face.

On January 11, 2018, at approximately 11:00 a.m., an employee was attempting to drive an ATV up a steep incline when it tipped over backwards. He was hospitalized with a fractured lower vertebra and internal bleeding.

An employee was tripping drill pipe out of a hole at a drilling rig when he tripped and put his hands out to catch himself. While his hands were on the ground, the pipe fell on and cut his right pinky finger. His pinky finger was surgically amputated at the knuckle.

An employee was attempting to help a rig crew attach an extended boom to a front-end loader. He was trying to push the retaining pin on the front-end loader back in when the operator activated the ram lever, causing the pin to close on his right thumb. His right thumb was amputated at the knuckle and he was hospitalized.
An employee was conducting well-servicing operations when he injured his back.
An employee was delivering fuel to a store when his pants caught on fire. He sustained burns to both legs and his left hand.
An employee was performing maintenance on a remote seismic vibrator when his right pinky finger became caught in the locking mechanism, amputating it at the first knuckle.
An employee was troubleshooting a pump and opened a plug valve. When the valve opened, pressurized water came out and struck the employee's left hand, puncturing it.

Employees were rigging down a well-servicing rig as an operator station was being lowered with a winch line. The operator station became temporarily hung up on the gears, causing the winch line to develop approximately 4 feet of slack on the line. When the operator station freed itself, it fell approximately 4 feet and struck an employee. The employee suffered fractured vertebrae.

An employee was rigging down a workover rig from the operator's platform when the scoping ram hydraulic system failed, allowing the mast to fall to the ground. The employee fell approximately 45 inches off the rig platform to the ground, suffering fractures to the leg and face.
An employee broke a leg while working as a floor hand on a well servicing rig.

On January 18, 2018, at 5:40 p.m., an employee was in a boatswain chair greasing blocks when the safety hook came undone, causing the employee to fall 15 to 20 feet to the rig floor. He fractured his right arm and some ribs, requiring hospitalization.

An employee was attempting to change a gear belt on a motor that had seized on a pumping unit when the belt started moving and caught his thumb, lacerating and breaking it. The motor was not locked/tagged out at the time of the incident.
An employee fell from the top of a truck and landed on the ground, breaking his leg in two places and requiring surgery.

On January 21, 2018, an employee was rigging down rig stairs to be picked up by a mobile equipment telehandler. While the telehandler was scoping out to pick up the rig stairs by the handrails, the forks bounced and struck the employee on his left shoulder. He suffered pain and numbness on the right side of his body, as well as inflamed bulging discs.

An employee was driving a street sweeper down a well pad access road when he applied the brakes, slid into a ditch, hit a mound, went airborne, and rolled two times. He suffered fractured ribs, a collapsed lung, and a fractured pelvis.
An employee was grabbing a transfer cup to place it on top of a rod when his thumb became caught in the transfer cup's hole, amputating it.

An employee was using a hydraulic torque wrench to tighten bolts on a flange. The employee's left hand was near the head where the hydraulic hose connects to the wrench. The hose became punctured and injected the employee's left-hand palm with hydraulic fluid, lacerating it.

An employee was adjusting a "T" attachment on a loader to carry a bundle of guide rods. The driver of the loader exited it and bumped the steering wheel, causing the "T" attachment to shift. The employee's hand was then caught between the guide rod bundle and the "T" attachment, partially amputating his right ring finger.

An employee had been in a derrick helping a snubbing unit crew change out a stiff arm. He was coming down from the derrick when the snubbing unit dropped the short stiff arm, which then caught his left index finger against the handrail. He suffered an open compound fracture to his finger.
An employee was helping spot a tractor trailer and was caught between the trailer and flatbed resulting in a fractured pelvis.
An employee was pressure washing in an acid tank tanker and sustained chemical burns.
An employee slipped while getting off a skid steer, breaking a leg.

An employee was hooking up a hydraulic hose to a blowout preventer beneath the work floor when a clamp on the cable holding the rig floor broke, causing the rig floor to fall. The employee was pinned between the rig floor and the blowout preventer, suffering a facial fracture.
An employee was bleeding down an injector line to bring a well back online when the line blew at a 90-connection. A 14-foot, 6-inch section of pipe blew out and broke the employee's tibia/fibula.
An employee was using a pipe wrench to loosen a fitting on a hot oil truck when the wrench slipped and amputated his left index finger.

An employee was tripping pipe (drilling the pipe down) and screening a drill collar into a stump. He and another employee pushed the tongs into the spinning pipe. The tongs then bit back, crushing him between the tongs and the derrick leg. He received fractures to his upper torso and punctured both lungs.

An employee was in a harness and was raised in the air with a winch line to remove a T-valve on top of a pipe. As the operator raised him up, the counterweight of the winch became caught on the tubing board and built up tension on the winch line. As the tension built up on the winch, it gave way and catapulted the employee through the air. The employee suffered pelvic injuries.

An employee was trying to light a burn box, but the ignition switch was not working. The employee used a hand torch to ignite the burn box, and the flames flashed in his face, causing first and second degree burns.

An employee was performing maintenance on the frac pump and was using a pry bar to roll the pump for re-packing. The pry bar slipped and struck the employee's head. He then fell striking his head on the ground and sustained a concussion.
An employee was opening an oil valve at a client site. Pressure blew the employee off the platform and onto piping below resulting in a fractured back.

An employee was sitting on a haul trailer when an ATV backed into him pinning him against the haul trailer. The employee was hospitalized for a fractured right femur, a broken nose and a one-inch laceration on his right check.
An employee was moving a large job site tool. The tool fell and caught his right hand resulting in amputation of the pinky fingertip.

An employee was attempting to raise the tongs up off the rig floor with a hoist when a safety pin became hung on the floor grating. The employee had his hand on the tongs while trying to see what they were hung up on. At that time, the tongs came free from the floor grating and caught the employee's left pinky finger between the tong body and mid rail resulting in amputation.

An employee was using a telehandler to move cargo when a front loader lost traction at the top of a hill and slid down into the telehandler as the employee was trying to get out, crushing his right leg and pelvis.
During rig down operations, an employee's left index fingertip was amputated.

An employee was on the back of a goose neck flat bed trailer approximately four feet high unloading racks made out of pipe. As he started to unbind chains on two racks they slipped and started to fall. The employee then fell off the trailer to the ground and was pinned between two racks. The employee suffered an abdominal injury as a result of the incident.
An employee was driving to an oil and gas site and drove into a river/ditch.

An employee was replacing a valve in a process line using a chain fall. The employee's finger was caught between the new valve and the top of the flange crushing it and resulting in a partial amputation.
An employee was moving the bridle from a pumping unit when a brake gave way, catching the employee's right pinky. The employee's right pinky fingertip was amputated.

An employee was manually moving a pump jack to a neutral position so he could grease the gears when his right index and middle fingers were pinched between the belt and a pulley. His right index fingertip was amputated above the first knuckle and his middle fingertip was crushed.
Employees were cleaning out a shaker trough with a pressure washer when hydrogen sulfide gas released from the shaker. Two employees were hospitalized due to gas exposure.

An employee was emptying a filter pod at the flare stack when a small flame came out of the top of the flare stack, landed in the condensate, and burned him. He suffered second degree burns to the hands, stomach, and calves, requiring hospitalization.

An employee was using a spray wand connected to a hot water pressure washer to open up a frozen produce water tank. The produce water vented hydrocarbon vapors near the hot water pressure washer causing a fire. Two employees received second and third degree burns to the face, neck and hands.
An employee was lifting pipe out of the wrangler. The pipe slipped out of the elevator and struck the employee in the face and shoulder. The employee was knocked unconscious.
An employee was walking into the dog house to warm up and closed the door on her hand resulting in a fractured right thumb.
An employee was changing liners in the mud pump and got his right index finger smashed between the liner and sledge hammer.
An employee was moving a rug when she fell forward and sustained a hairline fracture of the right hip.

Employees were replacing a pump at a gas well site. After set up, the pump jack was not pulling gas from the well. A cable was hooked up to the pump jack to move it slightly. As the cable was pulled, the pump jack tipped over onto an employee breaking the employee's tibia and fibula.

An employee was walking over to check for leaks on a gauge. The employee noticed three lines/hoses had collapsed. The blender was on and when the valve opened 100 pounds of pressure hit the hoses causing them to jump up and strike the employee breaking the right tibia and fibula.
An employee sustained a laceration to the right leg above the knee while pressure washing shaker pits with an industrial pressure washer.
Employees were hoisting drilling pipe, when the pipe fell, striking the back of an employee who was standing on the rig floor. The employee sustained fractured ribs and vertebrae.

An employee was checking the coolant level in a radiator for one of the rig's generators. When he twisted the radiator cap, the cap came off and he was sprayed with hot coolant resulting in burns to his right arm, shoulder, chest and scapula. Immediately afterward he ran towards the rig manager's trailer and while doing so tripped and fell resulting in a broken right clavicle and cracked scapula.
An employee was walking back to the trailer after conducting maintenance outside when he slipped on ice and fell to the ground, fracturing his left hip.

An employee was getting the loop out of a drilling line at a spool when the driller started the spool, catching the employee's right hand between the line and spool. The employee's right ring and index fingers were amputated.
An employee was descending stairs from a tank battery, slipped on an icy step and fell about halfway down the stairs, fracturing the left fibula.

Three employees nippled up a blowout preventer's operation while standing in ankle-deep water that had cement residue in it. Later, one of the employee's suffered first, second, and third degree burns to his feet, requiring hospitalization. Rubber boots were not worn at the time of the incident.
An employee was working on the cylinder of a trailer, attempting to loosen the bolt with a pipe wrench, when it loosened unexpectedly and he slipped onto the floor, breaking his lower left leg.

A team on the rig floor was attempting to rig down a cement head with a manifold assembly from the rig floor down the slide to the ground below. A winch line was being used to lift the cement head off the rig floor to allow the team members to push the head to the slide. The head was pushed out beyond the slide, but the manifold caught on the rig floor and the head swung back toward the floor and struck the swing gate. An employee was holding the swing gate open with his right hand and was struck on the pinky finger. The distal interphalangeal joint was partially amputated.
An employee was working with a Kelly swivel to move pipe joints on the rig floor. His coverall became wrapped into a rotating joint and the employee sustained a fracture to the left forearm.

An employee was setting a packer on a flatbed trailer to connect and thread the pipe when the employee's hand slipped and the pipe fell on it, trapping a finger between the pipe and the edge of the trailer. The employee sustained a right ring finger amputation.

While conducting rig-up operations, two employees were carrying a 2-inch joint of iron piping when the first employee dropped the joint on the second employee's finger. His right middle finger was crushed between the falling pipe and piping that was on the ground, resulting in an amputation.

An employee was operating a skid steer over rough terrain when he hit a culvert, which jerked the skid steer. The abrupt motion caused him to hit his head against the rear window of the cab, fracturing his skull and requiring hospitalization.

An employee was helping to load a BOP component on a tractor trailer when the tractor trailer operator started to move the truck. The employee jumped off the trailer to avoid being struck by the BOP and struck the ground, breaking the right knee.
An employee was rolling pipe when his right index finger was pinched between two pipes, resulting in an amputation.
An employee was helping to lay down pipes on a work-over rig's pipe wrangler when a pipe jumped out of the wrangler and struck his side, breaking four ribs. He was hospitalized.

A crew was rigging down when a weight bucket became hung up while the derrick was being scoped in. One of the employees pulled on the cable, causing the climbing assist weight to come loose and descend toward him. As a result, he let go of the line and was struck by the weight. He suffered a right arm fracture, broken ribs, and lacerations to his left gallbladder and kidney.
An employee was flagging a forklift operator while he picked up a pipe rack to be moved. The pipe rack fell from the forks of the forklift and landed on the employee's feet, crushing both.
An employee was watching the wrench. When the wrench moved, the employee's hand was caught resulting in a partial amputation of the right ring finger.
An employee was moving a panel switch to the open position on a 480-volt motor control center breaker when an electrical arc flash occurred, burning the employee's eyes, face, neck, and hands.

An employee was repairing a well. He was connecting a polish rod to a rod string and stuffing box. The box was 3 inches above a pipe wrench that was on the polish rod. The employee's hand was on the pipe wrench when the stuffing box slipped down onto his left index finger, crushing it and resulting in an amputation.
An employee was struck by a truck that was reversing to hook up a trailer, suffering back and hip injuries.
An employee was bleeding down the well in the process of plugging an abandoned well when the valve blew apart resulting in a lower left leg fracture.

An employee was releasing 9,500 PSI pressure by surging a 2-inch 1502 iron bleed-off line when the bleed-off iron shifted and struck his right leg, fracturing his foot and ankle. He was hospitalized and had surgery.

An employee was taking samples and reading gauges when the sight glass blew out on a flake caustic line. The blow-out caused lacerations to the employee's arm, face, and chest and chemical burns to his face and right hand.

A generator was being replaced on a drilling rig. The 3700 pound generator was lifted and held with a chain attached and carried by an all terrain forklift. While the injured employee was pushing the generator with two other employees, the chain holding the generator slid from the forks of the all terrain forklift and fell backwards onto the employees. The injured employee sustained rib fractures.
Two employees were involved in a physical altercation at the work site. One employee suffered a broken nose and was hospitalized.

An employee was using an outrigger for balance while he used his foot to clear snow from the area where the outrigger foot would sit. While the employee's hand was on the outrigger, the outrigger activated. The employee's right index finger that was inside a pin hole when it moved resulting in amputation.

An employee was making a connection with a drill pipe and had a hand around the pipe when it moved into an iron roughneck. The employee's right pinky finger was caught between the iron roughneck and pipe, amputating the fingertip.

An employee was adjusting the sliding support on a trailer (150 pounds) when the employee's right index finger was caught between the slide and trailer, resulting in a right index fingertip amputation.
An employee was on a catwalk when it broke loose at the mounting points, causing the employee to fall 12 feet to the ground and suffer a shoulder injury.

An employee was troubleshooting a problem with a chemical pump. During a fracturing operation, the employee disconnected a chemical hose that was under pressure. Chemicals released and entered the employee's right eye, causing a chemical burn.

An employee was pumping water down tubing to get mud back to a frac tank. When the pump pressured up, the inner rubber of the hose came apart, plugging the hose and causing it to blow out of the tank. The hose then struck the employee's wrist and chest.
An employee was performing unloading activities when a 4-inch cap flew off an undrained vent-and-fill line and struck the employee's head.

An employee was exiting a rock crusher and getting onto a 6-foot step ladder. He was holding onto the handrail while getting his feet onto the ladder. His feet were on the second rung from the top when the ladder kicked out from underneath him. He held onto the handrail momentarily and then fell 4 to 5 feet to the ground (gravel pad), breaking his left wrist and suffering a small compression fracture in his lower back. He was hospitalized.

An employee was working on the rig floor assembling a bottom hole assembly when a shock-sub struck the top of his right foot, damaging his pinky toe. His toe had to be surgically amputated from the last joint.

An employee was setting a pin in a boom to connect two sections. When the employee went to hit the pin with a sledgehammer, his hand slipped and the sledgehammer struck his hand, fracturing his finger and resulting in an amputation.

An employee was inspecting a pressure relief valve on a unit when the relief valve discharged heated gas into the employee's face. The employee suffered a corneal abrasion and superficial burns to the face.
A crew of employees were cleaning a site to prep it for oil rig drilling work. While lifting debris from the ground, one employee was bitten by a cotton mouth snake, requiring hospitalization.

An employee was standing on a porch that was 13 feet from the ground and was tying off to a hand rail when another employee from a different company took out the pin that stabilized the porch. The porch swayed, causing the employee to fall to the ground. The employee suffered a broken collarbone, four broken ribs, one lung bruise, and a head injury that required stitches.
An employee was using a hammer on a stuck valve when the hammer broke. A metal shard from the hammer pierced the employee's eye.

A crew was in the process of putting a sub-spreader beam in place so that they could raise the rig floor. An employee's hand was resting on the spreader beam when the derrick hand pulled the beam from its stowed position. The employee's small finger was then caught between the spreader beam and the sub leg, amputating his fingertip.
An employee slipped and fell on ice in the parking lot. He injured his knee and required surgery.

An employee entered a tower and was vacuuming out adsorbent that was stuck to the inside walls when the adsorbent became detached from the wall and engulfed the employee. The employee suffered upper body trauma and partial asphyxiation, requiring hospitalization.
An employee was operating a service rig when a natural gas explosion and fire occurred, burning the employee's face and neck.

An employee was helping to remove wind screens from around the rig when his right little finger was caught between a wind screen and an eye on the side of the doghouse. His right little fingertip was partially amputated.

An employee was standing on the rig floor when a chain broke while cement was being piped into the casing. The broken chain struck the employee on the hard hat resulting in a laceration and a possible eye socket fracture.

An employee was working on a centrifuge on top of a centrifuge stand. The employee lost footing while stepping down from the centrifuge and fell backward into the handrails. The hand rails gave out, causing the employee to fall approximately 12 to 15 feet to the ground. The employee suffered bruised muscles and a pinched nerve in the buttocks.

An employee was sliding a mechanical seal/sleeve onto a shaft. The shaft has a small groove with sharp edges. The employee's hand was on the shaft with his finger in the groove. When the employee slid the mechanical seal/sleeve on the groove, it amputated his right index fingertip.

An employee was attempting to attach a lifting clamp to a steel flange plate when the plate fell approximately 6 inches, pinching his fingertip between the ground and the plate. As he pulled his hand out of the pinch point, the fleshy part of his fingertip ripped off of his finger.
Employees were unlatching a trailer when the trailer moved, catching the injured employee's left index finger between the truck and the trailer hitch. The employee's fingertip was amputated.
An employee's left hand was inside skid rail pin holes checking the alignment when the skid rail moved backwards and amputated his left middle and index fingertips.
An employee was making collars to go into the hole at an oil drilling rig when the drill collar tongue struck the middle part of the employee's body.
An employee was injured when a candy cane in a Poseidon tank came loose and a ratchet strap that was holding the candy cane struck and lacerated his arm.

An employee had cleaned drill pipe threads with rags containing chemical cleaner and then threw the rags into the back of a work truck. Exhaust from a generator inside the truck ignited the rags. The employee grabbed the rags and his coveralls caught fire. He received burns to his hands, stomach, thighs, and lower legs.

An employee was attempting to load a derrick board onto a flatbed haul truck with a forklift. His hand was between the forklift fork and derrick board as he tried to remove a rope from the bottom section of the derrick tarp. The derrick board then shifted, catching his right hand and wrist between the derrick board and forklift fork. He suffered fractures to the right wrist and hand.

An employee was trying to come off a well and was laying a tool string to lay up for another run. His hand was on the wireline when the bottom sheave was raised and pinched his right ring finger, resulting in an amputation.
An employee was disassembling a butterfly valve and using a ball-peen hammer to remove the seal insert when the hammer struck and amputated the employee's left pinky fingertip.

An employee was checking a power swivel's back-up securing line to see if it was tight enough. As he reached out to slap the line, residual stored energy released, causing the securing line to back spin. The line was attached to a turnbuckle with a safety pin in place. The safety pin spun backwards, catching and lacerating the employee's right inner elbow area and causing potential muscle damage.

An employee was holding a 55-gallon drum in place with his right leg while another employee was attempting to puncture the drum with the forks of a forklift. As the forklift operator applied pressure to the drum with the forks, the injured employee's foot became pinned to the ground under the drum, resulting in a fracture to his right leg. He was hospitalized and had surgery.
An employee was steaming out a line when a candy cane propelled out of the tank, striking the employee in the head and hands. The employee suffered a facial cut, facial burns, and a broken hand.

An employee was standing on a piece of equipment to assist in a maintenance task when a second employee inadvertently started the equipment. The injured employees' left foot then became caught and fractured in a rotating piece of machinery. The equipment was unguarded at the time.

An employee was using a cart to push a turbine diaphragm out of a temporary sandblasting tent when the wheels encountered sandblasting grit on the floor, which stopped the progress of the cart. When the cart stopped, the weight shifted, causing it to tip over and the diaphragm to fall on the employee s right leg, breaking it.

Two employees were trying to loosen a bolt to disassemble a coupler between an engine and compressor. One employee was on the engine side while the other (the injured employee) was on the compressor side holding a shim. When the employee on the engine side turned the bolt for the coupling assembly, the engine crank rolled and amputated the injured employee's left middle fingertip.
An employee was standing in the top dog house of a drilling rig when a 3/8" plug shot out of a jar tool and struck him, injuring his left bicep. He was hospitalized.
An employee was removing debris from the job site and was on a digger derrick dumpster truck when he fell off the truck edge to the ground, fracturing his patella and lacerating his forehead.
Employees were using a forklift to raise a conveyor. The straps attached to the forklift forks slid off and the conveyor fell onto the employee's left foot fracturing the tibia and fibula.

An employee was inserting a hand held wand with a burning cloth attached to the end into a 4" opening of the main burner valve to ignite the pilot. The flame ignited residual gas and burned the employee.

Employees were cutting steel pipe into sections. A backhoe bucket was holding pipe about two feet above ground level. Employees had cut pipe on the west side and walked to the east side to cut sections. When the crew arrived on the east side, the backhoe lifted the pipe an additional two feet in preparation to start jarring the pipe to complete the cut on the west side. As the backhoe was lifting the pipe, the pipe on the west side broke completely causing the pipe on the east side to swing north hitting an employee and causing him to fall. The pipe landed on the employee's left knee. The employee was hospitalized with a broken left knee that required surgery.
An employee was walking in the lobby of an office building when she fell and broke her hip, requiring surgery.

An employee was about to go down a flight of stairs but noticed someone coming up the same stairs. He then re-directed to go to another set of stairs but tripped and fell. He shattered his left elbow and was hospitalized.
An employee was handling a piece of pipe when it slipped and caught his right pointer finger between the pipe and trailer, resulting in a fingertip amputation.
An employee was caught between a sand truck and a sand bin while serving as ground guide/spotter on location. He suffered a laceration on his left inner thigh, requiring surgery.

Employees were rigging down and started removing fluid from a line. They placed a clamp at one end of the line, but the clamp loosened and two employees were struck. One employee was hospitalized with internal injuries.

An employee was cutting pipe at a wellhead when a pocket of oil suddenly surfaced (well was plugged). A flash fire then occurred, causing second to third degree burns to both of the employee's hands and the right side of the stomach. PPE was not worn at the time of the incident.
An employee was cleaning out a piston on a chemical pump and amputated the right index finger to the fingernail in a pinch point between the piston and the cylinder.
An employee was working on a pipe rack arm when it slipped and pinched the employee's left index fingertip, amputating it.
An employee was walking to his truck when he slipped in the mud and hit his head and back, suffering a concussion and spinal fracture.
An employee was grabbing a stand pipe from a 'V' chute to guide it when the pipe swung out. The employee then fell approximately 15 feet, breaking ribs and the hip.

On April 27, 2018, at approximately 7:00 AM, an employee was operating a drill and had just finished drilling two holes in some square tubing when he attempted to grab a shaving near the drill bit, which caught his glove. His left thumb was then pulled into the drill bit, severely cutting it and resulting in a partial amputation.

A crew was installing a top drive track during a rig move when it became hung up on a girt. The top drive track was freed and whipped, striking an employee in the head. The employee suffered broken right cheek bones, a broken jaw bone, and a right shoulder injury.
An employee was walking through a semi-wooded area when a rattlesnake bit the back of his leg.

An employee was performing maintenance on a pump at a gas well frac job. The employee removed the top cap off of the pump and removed the top valve. The employee went to remove the bottom valve and the pump stroked, catching and crushing the employee's right hand. The employee suffered a hand injury and was hospitalized.

An employee had unstrapped some downhole tools that were brought to a wellsite. While another employee was going to get a forklift, the load shifted and smashed his finger between the load and the rub rail, resulting in a finger amputation.
An employee was looking for a connection when he bumped into a 10-pound flow key and it fell on his ring finger, fracturing it.
An employee was loading tools on a truck when his left middle finger was caught and amputated between the truck bed and the bell.

An employee was ascending a set of stairs attached to a flowback tank. The employee placed his hand on the rail between a fixed section of the railing and a removable section of the railing. The railing shifted and his finger was pinched, resulting in a fingertip amputation.

An employee was removing a setting tool from the back of a truck when the tool began to fall. As he reached out to try and catch it, his finger was caught between the tool and the truck floor, resulting in a fingertip amputation.
Employees were switching railcars when one of the employees was caught between the two cars. He was crushed, suffering internal injuries to his upper abdomen and pelvic area.

Two employees were transferring rinsate from a chemical tote to frac tanks using a bucket. Approximately six hours later, both employees stated that they felt winded with slightly strained breathing. One of the employees was hospitalized due to strained breathing and low oxygen levels.

On May 8, 2018, at approximately 12:10 a.m., employees were running some traded pipes and casing. The crew had a problem connecting two pipes (casing), so they unscrewed those pipes and continued to work with the casing. The injured employee's left hand was on top of an open pipe when a hoist operator (driller) let a second pipe come down. The employee's left-hand fingers were caught between the two pipes (casing), resulting in an amputation of his index finger and a broken ring finger.
An employee was attempting to enter a pick-up when he lost his footing, fell, and struck his right side flank on the side step of the vehicle. He suffered a right kidney contusion and hematuria.
An employee was manually guiding valve stacks into place when the employee's left index finger was pinched, resulting in an amputation.

An employee on a work over rig went to the rig platform to relieve the rig operator. Wind was blowing very hard (30 to 40 mph) with gusts. An umbrella was attached to a handrail to protect employees from elements and blowing dust. The employee was adjusting the umbrella when a strong gust blew him off of the rig platform. The gust carried the umbrella, the 4-5 foot handrail, and the employee over the edge. He fell approximately 15 feet to the ground, breaking his femur.
An employee was operating a hydraulic pump when his left pinky fingertip was smashed in the valve, resulting in an amputation.

An employee was driving down a lease road when the employee struck a rock in the road, over-corrected, and ran off the road, striking larger rocks that set the airbag off. The employee suffered a possible concussion.

An employee was opening the forks of a forklift to pick up a bag of casing protectors when his left ring fingertip was partially amputated between the fork and the forklift carriage. Impact gloves were worn at the time of the incident.
An employee was walking in his working area when he slipped on mud and fell, injuring his leg.
An employee was checking the tong heads on some tubing tongs when the tongs engaged and amputated the first digit of the employee's left index finger.

On May 15, 2018, at about 4:40 p.m., two employees were using a forklift to transport a frac tank onto a flatbed trailer. The tank was placed on a metal plate positioned on the forks of the forklift. During transport, the frac tank and metal plate shifted, striking the two employees. One employee sustained two fractured knuckles to the left hand, requiring hospitalization.

An employee was offloading sand at a dust collection unit that was clogged. The auger was not rotating, so employees struck it with a hammer. The employee's fingers were inside the housing unit of the auger when it inadvertently began to rotate, crushing his fingers. He was hospitalized and had surgery.
A piece of wood/splinter from a wooden crate embedded in an employee's left thigh.

An employee was moving an 800 lbs. control panel onto a rig floor via forklift operations when the control panel became caught on a handrail, shifting the control panel from the strap. The control panel fell, striking the employee and then falling on top of the employee's left leg. The employee sustained a fractured left leg.

An employee was working on the rig floor while setting a casing when the employee lost balance and placed the left hand on the casing. At the same time, the casing slips were released and the inter-tool slid down, amputating the employee's left index finger at the first knuckle.

An employee went to sit down on a bench in a wire line support trailer when he felt pain in his left middle finger. He removed his gloves to investigate and noticed a puncture mark below the first knuckle on his left middle finger. The puncture later became infected, requiring hospitalization.

An employee removed nuts on a stripper head and was raising the head up over the annular when the head slipped and struck the employee's left arm, pinning it against studs. The employee's arms sustained multiple fractures.

An employee was trying to adjust brakes on a pulling unit and was installing a chain around the main drum. His left hand was on the chain when the drum moved, catching and smashing his left pinky between the drum and chain. He was hospitalized.
An employee was stung by a bee and had a severe allergic reaction.
An employee was observing pressure line testing, heard a hissing sound, stepped back to observe and fell into steel rebar. The employee was hospitalized for puncture wounds and internal bleeding.
An employee was hospitalized due to heat stroke after working in the equipment yard breaking down equipment.

Employees were releasing pressure from a well, moving lines from one well to another and placing a cap on the well-pumping lines. A crown valve was open and blew up. One employee sustained a broken right forearm, a second employee sustained a head injury and a third employee sustained an injury requiring surgery.

An employee was unscrewing a 2-inch iron elbow from a 2-inch iron straight pipe. The pipe shifted, and his left index finger was pinched between the elbow and the pipe. His left index finger was amputated at the first knuckle.

An employee was standing on some small pipes, lining the flange on the top of a pump skid on a foundation about 3 feet high. He lost his balance and went over the side of the skid, fracturing a vertebra in his neck.

An employee was attaching a wireline tool to a metal dolly after the tool had been lifted out of a well hole. The tool shifted on the dolly. The employee's right thumb was pinched between the tool and the dolly, and the end of the thumb was cut off above the first knuckle.
An employee suffered an injury while conducting normal duties on a well servicing rig.
An employee was struck by a tool while performing hydrostatic testing on a work-over rig. The tool impaled the employee, who required hospitalization and surgery.

An employee was running casing down. He was leaning with one hand on a slip and one hand on a guide bar that guides the casing down when he reached up and grabbed a roller without realizing it. The roller then rolled over and crushed his right pointer, middle, and ring fingers. Two fingers were amputated.
An employee was attaching a tong to a pipe when his left leg was caught in the tong pull line and the drill string, resulting in a left leg amputation.
An employee was performing rigging down to move the rig and began experiencing symptoms of heat-related illness including cramps.

An employee was sitting on the edge of a chute greasing the rams of a delivery system. The employee lost his balance and fell into the chute. As the employee fell into the chute, the chute doors closed fracturing both legs.
An employee was rolling a piece of drilling pipe when his left pinky was caught under the pipe resulting in a fingertip amputation.
An employee was stepping over a torque machine when he slipped and fell. He sustained a severe laceration to the arm and was admitted to the hospital.

An employee was securing a set of chains to the slip for the blowout preventer (BOP) when the tongs engaged causing the slip to grab pipe and begin to spin. The injured employee's right hand was caught between the slip and BOP, amputating the index fingertip.
An employee was pulling a hose that was stuck in mud and when it came loose the employee fell backwards breaking the right tibia.

On June 6, 2018, the injured employee was assisting in rigging up a load of tubing blocks. The equipment operator lowered the rig to pick up tubing blocks. The injured employee's hand was leaning on the blocks and when the load began to lift the injured employee's right ring finger became caught between the blocks and the chain/rig floor amputating it to the first knuckle.
A crew was slowly bleeding off pressure into the next section of valves when the Kelly hose burst and the hose struck an employee's leg causing a right tibia fracture.

An employee was working at a remote job site delivering chemicals. When he had finished delivering chemicals at that location, he began having a headache. The employee was looking for headache medicine in his backpack and removed a handgun from the backpack placing it on the truck console. When he later reached for the gun it discharged into his left hand. The employee was hospitalized and had surgery.
On June 10, 2018, at approximately 3:30 p.m., an employee suffered a partial amputation to the left middle finger while greasing the gears of the power tongs.

An employee was injured while positioning a trough for a well. The trough fell on the employee's right hand resulting in a fracture of the middle fingertip and lacerations to the middle and index fingers requiring stitches.
An employee was pinching a 10" nitro hose line and the line burst. The hose struck the employee flipping him and breaking his right tibia.

An employee was rigging up a piece of equipment when it began to roll and the employee was caught between the equipment and the subframe of a drilling rack. The employee suffered a broken right arm, broken vertebrae and the separation of muscles on the hip.
While changing a wiper rubber on the rig floor, an employee stepped on the Kelly (rotating piece of the floor) as it was moving and broke his right leg.

An employee was attempting to refill the fuel tank on a compressor in a trailer when the fuel tank cap pressurized and ignited gas vapors. The employee suffered first and second degree burns to the face, ears and nose.
An employee was working on a pump jack when his right hand was caught in the pump jack's belt, severing the first and second digits of his second and third fingers, as well as his thumb tip.
An employee was removing a drill stem from a drill stem rack and his right middle finger was caught in a pinch point created by the drill stem and a caliper resulting in a fingertip amputation.
An employee was operating a pipe handler when a drilling pipe was released and struck his right hand, resulting in a pinky finger amputation and fractures to the ring and middle fingers.
An employee was moving metal material when one of the employee's right fingers was caught between the material, resulting in a traumatic amputation of the fingertip.
An employee was grabbing a winch to make a pipe connection on the rig floor when his finger was crushed between the winch cable and the power swivel, partially amputating his pinky finger.

An employee was getting a well head to stop on the down side and the weights on top. He was trying to roll up loose cable running from the rod rotator to a Samson post. His hand was on the brake and he was watching the weights when he pulled back on the brake to stop the weights. His hand then struck the top of the cross bar of the weight guards and his finger was struck in the middle. His right thumb was pinched and injured, resulting in a thumb tip amputation.
An employee was working in an aerial lift to loosen a cam-lock trap when a cap struck the employee's face, requiring hospitalization.

An employee was taking a joint of iron off the back of a truck and rotating it back into the cradle where it was stored. A brace was missing; when the joint was put into its resting spot, it kept rolling, crushing the employee's left little finger against the work platform. The finger was amputated.

An employee was folding over a rain flap on a generator to pin it before an oil rig was moved. The employee's right middle finger was caught between a pad eye on the generator roof and a pad eye on the rain cap. The fingertip was amputated.
An employee experienced muscle cramps while rigging up isolation tools. The employee was hospitalized for dehydration.
An employee was attempting to wipe grease from a stay rod nut. A torque wrench (connected to another stay rod nut) engaged and pinched the employee's right little finger, amputating the tip.
An employee suffered a back injury while reaching into a cooler to retrieve a water bottle.

An employee was loading the engine pistons and cylinder liners onto a pallet to remove from the area for housekeeping purposes. He lifted the last piston by placing his fingers into the large holes on each side of the piston. The piston did not have rings installed on it. When he sat the piston (98 pounds) on the liner it slid into the liner catching two of his fingers between the piston and the liner, amputating the tips of two fingers on his left hand.
A metal valve attached to a flow line fell over, striking and lacerating the employee's left calf.

Three employees were moving a tool from the wash bay to two tool stands. The rear tool stand became caught on the lip of the floor and collapsed, causing the tool to fall off the stand. One of the employees attempted to catch the tool, resulting in it falling onto and amputating his left small finger.

An employee was inspecting pipe. The employee walked through a rack opening and was struck by a 4.5 inch pipe in the abdomen while the pipe was being passed through the rack. The employee suffered lacerations to the liver and bowels.

An employee was cutting the coke or removing the coke from the drum to the loading area. Steam was released during the coke cutting process and the employee suffered burns to the neck/jawline and hand/wrist areas.

Two employees were tripping pipe on the rig floor. One employee slipped, and his right index fingertip was caught between the matting and the pin end of the pipe. He was hospitalized; the tip of his right index finger was amputated.
An employee was lining up a rig auger and kelly when the equipment shifted and made contact with his right index finger, resulting in a partial amputation.

A Lone Star Wolf Service employee was testing tubing going into a well when he began helping an operator who was lowering testing bars and pressuring them up for testing. After a couple of repetition runs of inserting the testing gun into the testing bar eye and hydrotesting the tube, the operator lowered the bars a bit more to have a complete seal. At the time, the injured employee's hand was on the testing gun handles, and his right index finger was pinched between the wiper cup and the testing pan. He was hospitalized.
An employee was helping to direct a traveling block off the ground. As the block was being raised, his left foot was caught between it and a well head, and was lacerated and broken.

An employee was operating a blender. Noticing that a booster pump was running, he began walking toward it to turn it off. The booster pump deadheaded, causing pressure and steam to build up in the line, and as the employee approached an 8-inch suction hose broke loose from the pump and struck him in the lower left leg. He suffered a compound fracture to the left leg and second-degree steam burns to the torso.
An employee was organizing a Conex box when his right ring finger was caught between a hose and metal shelf in the box, resulting in a fingertip amputation.
An employee was working on a drilling rig location, adjusting and pushing forklift blades, when the blades pinched the employee's middle finger, resulting in a fingertip amputation.
An employee was using a manual wrapping machine to wrap pipe for an oil field when he tried to manually adjust the machine and his hand was pulled into it, breaking his right forearm.

An employee was operating a pump supplying water for a fracturing operation (oil/gas) when the pump's discharge hose disconnected, and the hose clamp securing the hose to the flange failed. The hose then struck the employee's right shoulder, upper right back, and pelvis. The employee suffered two fractures to the pelvis, contusions, and abrasions, requiring hospitalization.
An employee was working in an area with an open-ended line when hot steam/water splashed on his back.

An employee was working with another employee, torqueing the manways on a tower. He came down around 2:30 p.m. due to the weather and went back up around 3:30. Around 4:45 the two finished the job. They came down and walked back to the lunch tent to rest, at which point the employee began vomiting. He was hospitalized for heat-stress-related illness.

An employee was about to climb a 15-foot chain ladder to exit a horizontal vessel. When he stepped onto the ladder, it became unstable and he fell. He landed on his back on the vessel's floor, suffering multiple broken vertebrae.
An employee was driving a pole truck. The truck contacted a power line resulting in burns to the employee's right arm and leg. The employee was hospitalized.

A crew was working to remove tubing from a well. A 2-inch hose was connected to the tubing for fluid circulation. The crew was raising the tube when the hose was caught and came under tension. An employee attempted to dislodge the hose, which reacted and sprung into the employee's face, breaking bones. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was removing a 2" riser pipe from a casing head with a pipe wrench when backside pressure pushed the riser up and it struck the employee's forehead. He was then covered in drilling mud, which evacuated the well behind the pipe. He suffered a forehead laceration and skull fracture.
An employee sustained a partial amputation of the left middle fingertip while opening the access door on a filter pod.

An employee was changing a leaking valve on a POD with a wrench. While he was loosening the bolt, the wrench slipped off the bolt and his right middle finger was pinched between the wrench and the edge of the equipment, resulting in a fingertip amputation.

An employee unloaded two pipe racks off a flatbed trailer, set them aside, and climbed on the trailer to remove the chains from the other racks. The employee then climbed off the trailer and began walking back toward the cab on the driver's side when a pipe rack rolled off the trailer and caught the employee's left thigh, fracturing the left femur.

An employee was standing in the work area waiting for a pipe fitter to lower when the pipe fitter, which was hoisted on a chain, became dislodged and struck the employee's left leg. The employee sustained a fractured fibula and tibia, requiring hospitalization.

On 7/13/2018, an employee climbed an 8-foot A-frame ladder to tape an area for painting. The employee finished and was starting to descend when the employee missed one of the ladder rungs and fell to the ground. The employee suffered a head cut and broken right ankle, requiring hospitalization and surgery.
An employee was on a drilling rig when the shaker tank's overflow line hit and tripped the employee, who fell down stairs off the rig floor. The employee suffered a fractured right tibia and fibula.
An employee was working on a frac tank and fell into the guardrail resulting in injury to the left torso/ribs.
An employee was working on the work-over rig floor when he slipped on some hydraulic fluid and fell into casing tongs, injuring his head and shoulder.
An employee was removing the lower section of a valve. The pump plunger came forward and pinched the employee's finger, causing an amputation.
An employee was using tongs to pull a pipe out of a hole when he lost his grip on the tongs and they swung around, striking him. He suffered two pelvic fractures and a tear in his bladder.
While replacing a transformer fan motor, an employee was shocked through the shoulder and out the chest. The employee lost consciousness.

An employee was holding bushing pullers while attempting to set bushings when he was struck on his lower back area with a bushing puller (an approximately 1 inch X 2 feet metal device connected to a hoist for lifting). He suffered a spleen injury that required surgery and hospitalization.

An employee was struck on the right elbow by a rod wrench while he was backing off a rod coupling. He suffered an open laceration and non-displaced fracture to the right elbow, as well as a fracture to the left index finger. He was hospitalized and had surgery.

An employee was working outside on July 17, 2018, preparing for the next day's job when he started not feeling well. The next day, July 18, 2018, the employee was at a customer location working and started vomiting and was unable to keep any fluids down. The employee was hospitalized for heat exhaustion and renal failure.
While flushing chemical from a tanker truck an explosion occurred that burned three employees. One of the injured employees was hospitalized with burns to the face and hands.
An employee was laying down casing. The casing elevators opened and the 7" casing fell onto the employee. The employee sustained a fractured shoulder and ribs and head trauma.

An employee was attempting to clean a tank when the air distribution system was activated, causing the solution (hot water mixed with a 10% concentration of degreasing agent) in the tank to cavitate over the edge and land on the employee's neck, upper back, leg, right ankle, and chest. The employee suffered first and second degree burns.
An employee was working on a work-over rig. The employee climbed onto a derrick, about 5 feet above the ground, then slipped and fell to the ground. The employee's left wrist was fractured.
An employee was working at an oil well when his work truck failed to stay in park and rolled downhill, pinning him against a generator. His tibia and fibula were broken.
An employee was tripping pipe out of a hole when his right hand was caught between the handle and the elevator, injuring his index and middle fingers.

An employee was changing a bottom hole assembly and laying down a stabilizer and pony sub. Nearby rig hands could not get a pipe to a trowel. He saw they were in trouble with the pipe and attempted to help get the pipe to the trowel, but the driller did not land the pipe in the trowel. The pipe landed on the edge and rolled out, pinching him against a frame and stabilizer. He fractured his scapula and the spinous processes on his vertebrae.

An employee was acting as a ground guide for a rough-terrain forklift that was loading material onto a flatbed truck. The forklift's boom came into contact with overhead power lines while the employee was touching the forklift. The employee suffered electrical burns to his hands and feet.
An employee was retrieving his tools when he suffered a right pinky fingertip injury that later resulted in an amputation.
An employee was removing doors from an oil and gas treater with an electric impact gun. His tool arced and lit the gas in the room on fire, causing severe burns to both of his arms.
An employee had closed a plug valve halfway with a valve bar when he immediately felt a sharp pain in his lower back due to bulging discs that caused a pinched nerve.

An employee was undertaking a washout task on a skid when a hydrocarbon release was ignited by an unknown source. A flash fire burned the employee's lower back, face, neck, and hands. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was walking backwards, helping carry a section of perforating gun string to the gun stands on the ground. He tripped over a stand, falling backwards to the ground. The gun string came down on his right hand, breaking and lacerating his right ring and little fingers. He was hospitalized.

The governor on a portable welder had been replaced. While an employee was checking the wiring behind the governor, a coolant fan blade broke his left index finger and caused tendon damage and lacerations on the other fingers.

An employee lifted the lid to the glue cooling area of the machine to examine the equipment for issues. The lid covers two pulleys; one is 4 feet and the other is 16 inches in diameter. When he lifted the lid, it swung back and he raised his left hand to protect himself. He then lost balance and tried to steady himself with his right hand by placing it on the belt. His right hand got caught in the pulleys and when he pulled back, he suffered avulsions to his ring, pinky and middle fingers requiring hospitalization.

An employee was standing on the drum of an oil rig washing and removing grease from the drum when the operator activated the drum. The employee then fell between the drum and cable, fracturing his right femur.
An employee was making a connection when a heavy pipe got away from the employee and caught the employee's left forearm between it and a board.
An employee was hit by a falling sheave from a tester that was being placed in a well. The employee was struck in the chest below the collarbone, suffering a liver laceration and bruised lung.
A discharge hose failed, striking an employee and causing a laceration and fracture of the right tibia. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was disconnecting a pressurized hose from a truck when the hose popped off, causing the employee to fall backward on his left side. He broke his pelvic bone and was hospitalized.
An employee slipped while working on a blowout preventer, falling about 2 feet to the ground and suffering a broken thumb.
An employee was spotting a well servicing rig to a well when his right ring finger was caught between a wire cable and well-head bolt, resulting in a fingertip amputation.
An employee was working with tongues on the drilling floor when his hand entered a pinch point and the tongues caught his ring finger, resulting in an amputation at the first joint.
An employee amputated a pinky fingertip when it was pinched between a pipe and a stationary object.

An employee was part of a five-person crew that was removing a polishing rod when the clamp that holds the stuffing box failed, causing the stuffing box to catch the employee's hands against the clamp and stuffing box. The employee's right thumb was crushed, requiring hospitalization and surgery.
An employee was working outdoors and became ill due to heat exhaustion.
An employee was hospitalized after experiencing leg cramps.

An employee was operating a hose reel to rig up the swivel when his fingers were caught in the in-going nip point of the hose reel chain and sprocket drive, amputating his right pinky and ring fingers.
An employee pulled on a winch line, causing a horse head to slide down and strike the employee's right foot, fracturing it.

Two employees were working on a pump. The first employee had his hand in the pump when the second employee rotated the drive line. The rotating pump parts then caused an amputation to the first employee's right index finger and laceration to his middle finger.
An employee was bitten by a rattlesnake.
Am employee was removing sand that was jammed in an auger when the employee's right middle finger was caught in the auger, resulting in an amputation at the first joint.

An employee was descending a fixed ladder on the side of a blender when he attempted to step down to the next step and his hand slipped. He then fell 1 to 2 feet to the ground and tried to stop himself with his right hand, resulting in a fractured right arm.

An employee was setting up five mud tanks and a mud pump. While he was hooking up the fifth mud tank to the fourth mud tank, a gap formed between the hose to the union. He inched the cable over multiple times to close the gap. Then, the driver lifted the mud tank up, which caused the cable line to pull the employee's finger between the truck roller, resulting in an amputation of the end of his left index finger.

A spotter was directing a telehandler operator who was picking up an empty rack of piping. The operator picked up the load and did not see the communication from the spotter. As the operator was backing out, the spotter was crushed between the load and a parked trailer, fracturing his back.

An employee was standing on ladder reaching up to grab rods under the clamps. The rods lowered and pinched his thumb between the rod clamp and the rod rotator. The thumb was amputated below the second joint.
An employee was using a foot to set slips when the right foot was caught between slips and the rig floor, resulting in a partial amputation of the little toe.

An employee was attempting to depressurize a threaded natural gas line. He continued to disconnect the pipe and a significant pressure release occurred, dislocating his left shoulder and bruising his right thigh. He was hospitalized.
An employee was rigging up an isolation tool when he started to experience symptoms of heat exhaustion, requiring hospitalization.

While discharging pressure from and testing a well head, an employee opened a steel valve fitting under 400 pounds of pressure. The fitting unscrewed and was ejected, striking the employee's lower right leg and breaking it.
An employee was helping to build a fence. He reached down to pick up some fencing material when a rattlesnake bit him on the right hand through his gloves. He was hospitalized.

An employee was on the catwalk of a mixing plant at a completed well site. He was burned by a fire, centered on a forklift and a flowback tank that was releasing natural gas. He suffered second- and third-degree burns to his right hand and arm to the shoulder, his left hand, and his back on the right side. He also suffered second-degree burns to the right side of his face (excluding the eyes) and first-degree burns to his forehead. Personal protective equipment and flame-retardant pants were being worn, but not a flame-retardant shirt.

An employee was operating a tandem gin pole truck to assist with a load when the front of the truck began raising up and slammed down to the ground. He then exited the truck and laid on the ground in pain. He was hospitalized with an L2 vertebra fracture.
A flowback operator was cutting a hole in a 55-gallon poly drum. The knife closed on his left little finger, cutting it. He was hospitalized; the finger was amputated.

An employee was aligning/guiding a workover rig onto a well-head using a spacing cable when his left ring finger was caught between the spacing cable and the rod blowout preventer, resulting in a fingertip amputation.
An employee slipped and twisted his right ankle while attempting to carry a 50-pound bag of seed, fracturing his fibula and tibia.
An employee was collecting sweeps when he opened a gut line that was pressurized and the elbow failed, dislodging and hitting his back. He suffered the loss of his spleen and a collapsed lung.
An employee was collecting samples and his left hand entered a peach when the winch moved, resulting in a left index fingertip amputation.

An employee was disconnecting a braided metal flex hose that was supplying air to a furnace for the de-coking process. A supplier sent an alternate feed to the furnace, which required the furnace to remain online. The employee went to disconnect the flex hose from the furnace and received second degree burns to the face and first degree burns to the torso from steam/hot condensate. The line was not depressurized at the time of the incident.

An employee was part of a crew that was attempting to remove a Christmas tree from a well head when a high-pressure release and blowout occurred. The Christmas tree fell on and broke the employee's leg, requiring hospitalization.
An employee was adjusting a valve when the metal hinged door of a tank cage smashed his right thumb. The tip of the thumb was amputated.

An employee was lowering a pipe stabilizing tool called a "slip" into a drill hole/floor hole. As the drill was being lowered into the slip and drill hole, the employee's right foot lost traction and moved underneath the slip. The drill then entered the slip, which caused the slip to move and crush his right foot. His right big toe was severed at the first knuckle.
An employee was helping to take apart drilling equipment when an electrical arc hit a boom she was touching. She was hospitalized.
A piece of pipe slipped while being set down in a cradle and struck and employee's foot, injuring it.

An employee was helping guide a pipe into place to connect to rig equipment. His left hand was caught between the pipe flange and the rig equipment's frame, and his ring finger was pinched. The tip was amputated. Personal protective equipment and impact gloves were being worn at the time of the incident.
An employee was holding onto a pressurized hot water hose when hot water splashed onto the employee causing burns to their arms, chest and leg.
An employee stepped backward into a fueling pit on the ground that was about 2 to 3 feet deep, suffering a hematoma to his left leg just above his knee.

An employee of AROCK Services, LLC, was overexposed to hydrogen sulfide gas while changing a valve on a pumper unit. The employee experienced nausea and inflammation of the throat, requiring hospitalization.

A rig hand was guiding pipe to a racking system on a rig floor to rack back the pipe. He slipped and fell on the rig floor. As he fell, the 90-foot drilling pipe was stabbed into the floor of the rig, pinching his finger against the floor. His finger was partially amputated.

An employee was walking by a room where a subcontractor had been working on a pipe and heard a hissing noise that made him think that gas was leaking. He evacuated the room and told the subcontract workers to leave when the gas ignited. The employee received burns to his hands, face, and shoulders.
An employee was pinning the center section of a mast on a drilling rig when the pin was forced out of the pad eye connection and struck the employee on the right side of face, breaking bones.
An employee was removing tubing and sucker rods from a well when a sucker rod broke and fell, striking the employee. The employee was hospitalized with a fractured left arm.
An employee was operating the tongs at a rig when the winch line broke and the equipment struck the employee's lower right leg, breaking the tibia. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was tightening a new battery on a truck when the truck slipped off its jack. The employee's left leg was caught on the truck's battery box, breaking the leg and causing a laceration.
An employee was using pipe wrenches to disassemble a 16-gun assembly. After pulling a wire line out of the hole, the employee lost consciousness due to heat stress.
An employee was burned in an explosion that happened while a vacuum trailer was being power-washed.
An employee was holding several of an oil drilling rig's electrical cables while the rig was being transferred from one well to another. The cables were damaged, and the employee was shocked.

The injured employee was helping a welder while a nearby trackhoe operator had a 4' pipe joint hooked up to the trackhoe with a strap. The operator leaned forward to adjust his side mirror and as he sat back down, his shirt was caught on the joystick, which caused the machine to move the 4' pipe forward. It struck the 6' main line pipe, which in turn fell off the cones and landed on the injured employee's legs. Both legs were broken and she was hospitalized.

During the breaking of a connection, an employee was holding a "mud bucket" against a pipe to minimize the splashing of mud on an oil rig floor. As the two pieces of pipe were moved apart, a spray of mud caused the employee to fall and hit his head on a piece of equipment behind him. He suffered a scalp laceration and a skull fracture.
An employee was servicing an oil well. The employee's left hand was caught between a rod rotator and a bridle, and the little finger was amputated.

An employee was climbing the stairs on a coker unit to reach a crane cab. A drum of coke was cut open, releasing steam and hot gases; the employee suffered first-degree facial burns and second-degree burns to the left wrist.

An employee was on a blowout preventer (stationed on a pressure control trailer), using a wrench to align the tool trap. The wrench slipped and the employee lost his balance, falling about 7.5 feet and injuring his wrist, hip, and shoulder.
An employee was making a connection for drill collars when a tong struck him, breaking ribs. He was hospitalized.
An employee was walking through a containment, verifying chemical levels, when a chemical splashed onto his left calf. He suffered chemical burns and was hospitalized.

Two employees were driving on a lease road, hauling a pump. An antenna on the pump got caught on an overhead electrical wire, directing energy to the truck. One employee suffered an electrical burn, as well as a sprained ankle when he jumped out of the truck; the other suffered a shoulder injury when he jumped out of the truck and rolled on the ground.

An employee and a contracted forklift operator were moving matting boards that had been stacked in two piles. The top matting board in the shorter pile was forward and off center, leaving a gap between that mat and the taller pile of mats behind it. The employee was standing in the gap. When the forklift extended forward the lifting apparatus became caught on the off-center matting board and pushed it forward. The employee's right ankle was pinched between this mat and the pile of mats behind it, resulting in a broken right tibia and fibula.
An employee was setting up rig equipment and pinched his right middle finger between the pipe rack and the laydown machine index arm resulting in a fingertip amputation.

An employee was watching the hydrotesting of tubing to find a leak. A release of water from the tubing sent the employee back into the tubing board; the employee suffered broken ribs and injury to their spleen.
An employee was assisting with maintenance on the oscillator that was on a rack. The oscillator rolled and fell off the rack onto the employee's left foot fracturing it.

An employee was working with a crew, pigging a pipe. Built-up pressure shot out a small piece of steel pipe, which struck and lacerated the employee's left leg, resulting in an amputation below the knee. The employee was hospitalized.

Employees were trying to connect a wellhead with a two-to-one swedge and a quick coupler. A valve was opened to route pressure through the swedge. The swedge's threads stripped and it struck an employee in the ankle, fracturing it. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was bleeding down the pressure from a well to a vacuum truck when the gas fumes ignited, causing the employee to receive second degree burns to his hands and face.
An employee was talking with a truck driver when the employee was struck and fell under the truck. The truck/trailer ran over the employee, who suffered broken bones and internal injuries.

An employee was positioning a swivel into a cradle when the employee's right hand slipped and was caught in a pinch point between the swivel and cradle, resulting in an amputation to the right ring and pinky fingers.
An employee's forearm was injured by flying casing material in an explosion.
An employee experienced cramps and difficulty breathing after rigging up on location, requiring hospitalization for dehydration.

An employee had gone up a rig to unhook a block. The rig was clutched in, throwing the employee about 8 feet to the tuba line. His left knee struck a drum guard, which broke the kneecap. He was hospitalized.
An employee was rotating a multi-sample tool on a tool cart. The tool came off the cart and his middle finger was caught between the cart and the tool, amputating the fingertip.
An employee slipped on water, hitting the right side of her head on a countertop. She suffered a contusion on the right side of her head.

An employee was leaving an oil platform when he lost his balance while stepping over a centrifugal pump. He slipped off the skid to the ground about 6 inches below, twisting his ankle and suffering a broken fibula. He was hospitalized.

An employee was cooling off a radiator with a water hose. The radiator was uncapped, and the fluids inside it boiled off, burning the employee's torso; he fell to the ground and broke his right elbow. He was hospitalized.
An employee's clothing was caught by an uncovered rotating shaft. The shaft mangled the employee's left leg, which was amputated from the knee down.
An employee was hanging up a pump jack head. As the head was being lowered, it smashed the employee's hand against the pump jack. The employee suffered an amputation of the right forearm.
An employee was test-driving a go-cart he had been working on when it struck a parked car. He broke his left ankle and two ribs on the left side.
